vote_token.title: Use Vote Token / Give Up Vote Token
vote_token.text:
Definition

Vote token: the marker a player receives for voting when they die. A player gets 1 vote token when they die, and a dead player can only vote by using a vote token. Whether a player has any vote tokens, and how many, is public knowledge.

This differs from the official definition. In Odyssey, a player holding several vote tokens may spend them all on one nomination to cast several votes, or spend any number of them to cast that many votes. A player using several vote tokens at once shows the number with their fingers when raising their hand, so the Storyteller can count it. After counting, the Storyteller collects that many vote tokens.

Use vote token: a dead player voting with a vote token. Losing vote tokens other than by voting does not count as using them. This is public and visible to all players.

Give up vote token: a dead player (not a Traveller), during the day, publicly choosing a character to trigger its ability and handing their vote tokens to the Storyteller. The player loses all their vote tokens. A player with no vote tokens can't give them up. Giving up vote tokens is public, visible to all players, and only possible during the day. As long as a character whose ability involves giving up vote tokens is on the script, players may publicly choose it and give up their vote tokens even if it is not in play. If the script has several such characters, the player must say which character they are choosing; if it has only one, that step can be skipped.

Examples: 1. The dead Hanged Man votes with their vote token; when the game ends, good's win becomes evil's win. 2. Dead Townsfolk publicly choose the Skeleton King and give up their vote tokens; when the game ends, the Skeleton King wins, and so do those Townsfolk.

Related characters

Hanged Man, Pirate Cat King, Skeleton King

from_the_storyteller.title: From the Storyteller
from_the_storyteller.text:
Definition

From the Storyteller: a player privately learning some information, or getting some other item, from the Storyteller during the day. What they learn or get is secret and not visible to other players. A player with a "from the Storyteller" ability must approach the Storyteller themself to use it. Players without such an ability may also approach the Storyteller as a bluff, and the Storyteller will play along.

Examples: 1. The Paperboy approaches the Storyteller every day and privately gets a news story. 2. The Witness approaches the Storyteller every day and privately learns a piece of information. 3. The Riddler approaches the Storyteller on the first day and privately learns a riddle, but doesn't approach the Storyteller on later days and learns no new riddles. 4. Don Quixote approaches the Storyteller on the first day and privately learns who the Windmill is, but doesn't approach the Storyteller again and learns nothing new.

Related characters

Paperboy, Witness, Riddler, Don Quixote, Kappa

other_players.title: Other players
other_players.text:
Definition

Other (players): players other than the one with the ability — roughly the official "not yourself". There may be extra conditions, such as other good players, other Wolfboys or other Ettins.

Examples: 1. The Centaur and the Joker can only choose players other than themselves. 2. The Bug Catcher's ability only triggers when they nominate a player other than themselves. 3. A Wolfboy only becomes an evil Minion when a Wolfboy dies and only one Wolfboy is left alive (the other Wolfboys are all dead). 4. The Townsfolk the FaultBot checks don't include the FaultBot itself.

Related characters

Herald, FaultBot, Centaur, Bug Catcher, Wolfboy, Gargoyle, Loverbound, Ettin, Joker, Miko, Arbiter, Mermaid

judgment_day.title: Judgment Day
judgment_day.text:
Definition

Judgment Day: the first day of the game with fewer than 5 alive players (not counting Travellers). When Judgment Day begins, the Storyteller announces "Judgment Day has arrived" straight away. A game has at most one Judgment Day: if the game doesn't end on Judgment Day, later days are not Judgment Day even with fewer than 5 players alive. If the game ends early (a special win, or the Demon dying, say), there is no Judgment Day that game.

Before Judgment Day: the part of the game before Judgment Day arrives.

When Judgment Day arrives: usually the moment Judgment Day begins, when the Storyteller announces "Judgment Day has arrived".

After Judgment Day arrives: Judgment Day and the rest of the game after it.

If, on a day that is not Judgment Day, players die for some reason and fewer than 5 players are left alive (for example because of the Witch or the Golem, but not because of a normal execution), the Storyteller immediately announces Judgment Day. Abilities that trigger "when Judgment Day arrives" take effect at that moment (such as the Pirate Cat King and the Mummy). That Judgment Day ends at dusk, and there is no Judgment Day for the rest of the game.

A player feigning death counts as dead for Judgment Day.

Related characters

Pirate Cat King, Hydra, Blood Thief, Kraken, Mummy, Minotaur, Kappa

variable_x.title: Variable X
variable_x.text:
Definition

Variable X: X is a variable number in a character's ability, an integer set by some game state or condition. How X is determined is defined by each character's ability. For some characters X changes over time (the CodeX, the Crosswing); for others it is fixed once the game starts (the Venomtail). X is usually a non-negative integer. The X in different players' abilities are independent and calculated separately.

Examples: 1. On the CodeX's first night in play, X in their ability is 1; on their second night it is 2; and so on. 2. X in the Crosswing's ability depends on which night of the game it is. 3. X in the Venomtail's ability is set at the start of the game and doesn't change for the rest of it.

Related characters

CodeX, Venomtail, Crosswing

attack.title: Attack
attack.text:
Definition

Attack: a player with a Demon's ability, or the Storyteller, using that Demon's killing ability on a player. Usually an attack kills an alive player. Occasionally it doesn't — for example when attacking a player who can't die, or a player who is already dead.

Can't attack: a player with a Demon's ability is woken and told they can't attack because of an ability, then goes back to sleep. When the Storyteller decides the Demon's target, they can't attack anyone.

Can only attack: a player with a Demon's ability is woken and told, because of an ability, that they can only attack particular players. When the Storyteller decides the Demon's target, they too can only choose those players.

The term Attack comes from the official Fabled character the Toymaker and is defined in detail here (Odyssey only).

In most contexts "attack" describes a Demon's killing ability more briefly and plainly, as in "Each night*, attack a player" (an attack implies death). But since players are used to the official wording, Odyssey characters not closely tied to attacking keep the same ability wording as official characters.

Whether a player is poisoned or drunk doesn't affect whether an attack on them counts as an attack.

It includes delayed-death abilities like the Pukka's.

It doesn't include abilities that don't cause death, like the Leech's poisoning.

Examples: 1. The Storyteller uses the Yaggababble's ability to attack the Fool at night; the Fool is protected by their own ability and doesn't die. 2. The Imp attacks the Noble at night and the Noble dies. 3. The Pukka attacks the Tea Lady and poisons her; the Tea Lady dies the next night. 4. The Ronin protects the Fortune Teller and the Imp attacks the Fortune Teller that night; because of the Ronin's ability, the Baron is attacked instead and dies, and the Ronin regains their ability.

Related characters

Witcher, Ronin, MarMonk, Druid, Somnmaid, Nurgle, Arthur

delay.title: Delay
delay.text:
Definition

Delay: usually paired with an effect or state, as in delayed death. A delay postpones an effect or state on a player until the delay ends.

Delayed death: a player who would die doesn't die for now; their death is postponed until the delaying effect ends or disappears. Delayed death postpones deaths from execution and from character abilities.

A player whose death was delayed dies of the same cause as the first death they suffered during the delay. For example, if a player with delayed death is first attacked by the Demon and then executed, and the delay ends that night, they count as killed by the Demon's attack, since that was the first cause of death. (Except for the Witch Doctor; see the Witch Doctor's page.)

Examples: 1. Players the Demon kills die after the Valkyrie acts. 2. A player poisoned by the Witch Doctor doesn't die when executed, and dies as soon as they are no longer poisoned by the Witch Doctor.

Related characters

Valkyrie, Witch Doctor

traveler_isolation.title: Traveller Isolation Principle
traveler_isolation.text:
All Odyssey characters' abilities ignore Traveller characters and players when checking or resolving.

This includes: Travellers can't be chosen (the Joker and the Sensate can't choose a Traveller player); Travellers aren't learned (the Onmyoji won't learn a Traveller player); Travellers are skipped when counting positions (the Pearl Diver's and the Skipper's abilities ignore Travellers); actions taken by Travellers don't count (a Traveller nominating the Gargoyle doesn't die and doesn't count as the Gargoyle's "first nomination"; the Notary isn't woken on a night after a Traveller nominated and executed a player); and Travellers never count as particular players ("all evil players" in the Minotaur's, the Dretch's and the Blood Thief's abilities excludes Traveller players); and so on.

no_retroactive.title: About "retroactive" abilities
no_retroactive.text:
Odyssey characters don't use complex concepts like "retroactive" checks.

Characters whose operation involves placing tokens all work according to where the tokens are placed. If a token stands for information, the character is told that information when it gets its information. If a token marks a player, when the character gets its information the marked player is checked (their current state, not a past one), and the character is told the corresponding information.

Characters that don't use tokens are checked at the moment they act.

For characters that need a token placed in advance before they can act at night, if for some reason the token was not placed normally — for example the character entered play partway through — their ability can't trigger normally. For example: the Bard, the Lunar Knight.

For characters that don't expose anything publicly or create public effects, being poisoned or drunk doesn't affect where their tokens are placed. For example: the Dame, the Bard.

jinx_rules.title: Jinxes (special character interactions)
jinx_rules.text:
Jinxes are left to script writers: apart from specific character combinations that could badly break balance, which get a shared jinx, Odyssey leaves designing jinxes to script writers. They can design unique, imaginative jinxes of their own to suit their script's framework.

Hanged Man & Puck: if an evil player becomes the Hanged Man or gains the Hanged Man's ability (for example an evil Philosopher), they immediately lose that ability.

Hell's Outcast & Ettin: if the total number of evil players is already 1 more than at setup (not counting evil Travellers), "you immediately turn evil & swap characters with the Demon" in the Hell's Outcast's ability becomes "you immediately swap alignments and characters with the Demon".

Corruptus & Occultist: if the number of Outsiders in play at the start of the game differs from the default, the Occultist only learns false information this game.

More jinxes will be added over time...

painter.ability: You start knowing an in-play character. Each night*, choose a player: if they are the character you learned most recently, you learn another in-play character.
painter.summary: The Painter has to work out which players are the characters they learn.
painter.examples:
On the first night, the Painter learns the Noble. On the second night, the Painter chooses the Saint player and learns no new character. On the third night, the Painter chooses the Noble player and learns the Baron.

On the first night, the Painter learns the Noble. On the second night, the Painter chooses the Noble player and learns the Baron. On the third night, the Painter chooses the Baron player and learns the Imp.
painter.tips:
If you are the Painter, you can search openly early in the game for the character you learned, so that you get the next in-play character as soon as possible. But this is very dangerous: it immediately reveals that you are the Painter and invites trouble.

If you are the Painter, you can stay hidden early on. You might choose wrongly once or twice, but given enough time, players always end up revealing their characters.

If you are the Demon: a player who starts looking for a particular character on the first day is very likely the Painter. If you don't want them gathering lots of information too quickly, attack them at night.

If you are the Demon: a Painter who survives into the late game may know 2–3 or even more in-play characters, which is a huge blow to evil. If you find out who the Painter is, deal with them early.
painter.bluffing:
The Painter is a good bluff. You can use the Painter's ability as an excuse for never revealing your character. If you want to survive to the end, it is best to confirm the characters of 1–2 good players, so that they are more inclined to trust you.

If you are a Minion who isn't afraid of dying, you can announce that you learned several good characters, mixing your teammates in among them, which improves your teammates' chances of survival. Or you can go on the attack: claim that the characters you guessed correctly are evil, then accuse some players of being those evil characters. This is risky, but the payoff is huge: whether you are executed or the player you accuse is, you buy the Demon a lot of time.

witcher.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a player: they die, and the Demon can't attack tonight. If you kill the Demon, you & they swap characters & alignments.
witcher.summary: The Witcher can make the Demon's attack in the Demon's place.
witcher.examples:
On the second night, the Witcher chooses the Widow, and the Widow dies. When the Imp wakes, they learn that they cannot attack.

On the second night, the Witcher chooses the Vortox. The Vortox dies, the Vortox becomes a good Witcher, and the Witcher becomes an evil Vortox. That night, the new Vortox chooses a player, who dies.

On the second night, the Witcher uses their ability on the Widow, who is already dead, and the Vortox chooses the Chambermaid. The Chambermaid dies.
witcher.tips:
If you are the Witcher, your ability is very powerful: you can take over the Demon's job for one night and kill any player you like. Who to kill is the first thing to think about. A suspected Minion? Or the Demon, to become everyone's new nightmare?

If you are the Witcher, you can reveal early that you are the Witcher and then kill a player whom everyone thinks is evil, so that people are more inclined to believe you really are the Witcher. But this has a problem: if the player you choose is the Demon, you become the new Demon, and since you revealed yourself as the Witcher, the old Demon will certainly name you publicly as the new Demon. That all but guarantees you lose the game.

If you are the Witcher, you can hide your character until you have used your ability and are sure you didn't become the Demon, and only then reveal it. This is safer, but may be less convincing, because any evil player can claim to be the Witcher who killed last night's dead player.

If you are the Witcher, don't choose a dead player: if you don't kill anyone, your ability has no effect.

If you are the Demon and you can tell a player is the Witcher, try to kill them before they use their ability, so that they can't interfere with your evil plans.

If you are the Demon and you want a quick win at any cost, deliberately luring the Witcher into killing you is a "good" idea. If they fall for it, you are very convincing as a dead player and can almost certainly rally everyone to execute the new Demon the next day. You then win quickly as good — abandoning your evil teammates, of course.

If you are the Demon, don't be too afraid of the Witcher: at most they cover one night's shift for you and can't do much more. If you are the Po and you think the Witcher will use their ability tonight, hold your attack! The Witcher's ability then only speeds the game up.
witcher.bluffing: Have the Demon kill a player whom most players believe is evil, then come forward as the Witcher and say you killed them. You will be quite believable.

constable.ability: You start knowing a player. If you die at night, you learn a player. One of them is a Minion & the other is an Outsider. [+1 Outsider]
constable.summary: The Constable learns a Minion and an Outsider.
constable.examples:
Player 1 is the Baron and player 2 is the Damsel. On the first night, the Constable learns player 1. The Constable dies on the second night, is woken, and learns player 2.

Player 1 is the Saint and player 2 is the Poisoner. On the first night, the Constable learns player 1. The Constable dies on the second night, is woken, and learns player 2.
constable.tips:
If you are the Constable, you can share the player you learned early, so that everyone can work out together whether they are the Minion or the Outsider.

If you are the Constable, you can hide until you die at night. You then know an Outsider and a Minion, which is extremely important information: whichever of them claims not to be an Outsider is almost certainly the Minion. Even if you can't tell which of them is the Minion, at least neither is the Demon.

If you are the Demon, steer clear of the Constable: attacking them is not a good idea.

If you are the Demon and there seem to be more Outsiders than the default, be careful: the Constable is very likely in play.
constable.bluffing:
The Constable is not an easy bluff, because the ability adds an Outsider. Usually you need a teammate to claim an Outsider alongside you, or an ability of your own that adds Outsiders, to wear this bluff convincingly. Otherwise you may soon come under suspicion because the Outsider count doesn't add up.

If you are a Minion, you can claim that the Demon is the player you learned. If the other players trust you enough, they will conclude that player cannot be the Demon.

herald.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a player (not yourself): you learn 2 players. These 3 players are all different character types. [+1 Outsider]
herald.summary: The Herald can learn several players of different character types.
herald.examples:
Because the Herald is in play, there is 1 more Outsider than the default.

On the first night, the Herald chooses the Hatter player (Outsider) and learns the Fortune Teller player (Townsfolk) and the Poisoner player (Minion).

On the first night, the Herald does not use their ability. On the second night, the Herald chooses the Poisoner player (Minion) and learns the Imp player (Demon) and the Saint player (Outsider).
herald.tips:
If you are the Herald: of the 3 players you choose and learn, usually at least one is the Demon or a Minion — sometimes both!

If you are the Herald, share your information and work out as soon as possible which of the 3 players is the Townsfolk, which the Outsider, and which the Minion or Demon!

If you are the Herald: your ability adds an Outsider, so working out who that Outsider is matters a great deal.

If you are the Herald: if at least 2 of the 3 players claim to be Townsfolk or Outsiders, someone among them is lying!

If you are the Herald, you can wait a few days before using your ability. It is risky — you might die in the meantime — but if you wait, you will understand the game better: what everyone claims to be, and whom you find suspicious. You can then choose a confirmed Outsider or Townsfolk, which makes your information much stronger!

If you are the Herald, use your ability as soon as possible! You only get one chance, and if you die before using it, you will certainly regret it.
herald.bluffing:
Tell everyone that some 3 players are all different character types. That means at least one of them is evil (a Minion or the Demon)! It will spark a big discussion and shift the focus of the game.

Remember that the Herald's ability adds an Outsider. Usually, to bluff an extra Outsider, a teammate needs to help by claiming to be an Outsider.

If everyone thinks one of your teammates is evil, you can pretend you chose them, then name another teammate who is bluffing an Outsider plus a Townsfolk. This goes a long way towards helping that teammate pass as an Outsider.

Remember that the Herald can't choose themself.

bard.ability: Each day, you may publicly choose any number of alive players: the Townsfolk among them are drunk until you choose again. That night, you learn how many players are drunk due to you.
bard.summary: The Bard can make Townsfolk drunk, and learns how many Townsfolk that was.
bard.examples:
On the first day, the Bard publicly chooses 3 players, 2 of whom are Townsfolk. Those 2 Townsfolk are drunk from that moment, and that night the Bard is woken and learns "2".

On the first day, the Bard publicly chooses 3 players, 2 of whom are Townsfolk. Those 2 Townsfolk are drunk from that moment. That night the Demon kills the Bard; because the Bard dies, the 2 Townsfolk become sober and use their abilities normally that night.

On the first day, with the Vortox in play, the Bard publicly chooses 3 players, 2 of whom are Townsfolk. Those 2 Townsfolk are drunk from that moment. That night the Bard is woken and learns "0". The next day, the Bard publicly chooses an Outsider, and the 2 Townsfolk chosen earlier become sober.

On the first day, the Pit-Hag claims to be the Bard and publicly chooses 3 Townsfolk. That night the Pit-Hag turns themself into the Bard, but still nobody is drunk because of them, since they were not the Bard when they claimed to be.

On the first day, the Bard publicly chooses the Gambler, who is drunk from that moment. That night the Gambler chooses the Leper Gnome and immediately becomes a Leper Gnome. Since the former Gambler is now a Minion rather than a Townsfolk, they immediately become sober.
bard.tips:
If you are the Bard, talk to the players you intend to choose before you choose them publicly, so that you don't make an important Townsfolk drunk. You don't have to, of course, but you may then risk being executed outright.

If you are the Bard and you want to choose Townsfolk who use their ability during the day (such as the Fisherman), let them use it first. Otherwise your choice makes them drunk immediately.

If you are the Bard, encourage other players to claim the Bard too, so that the Demon has a hard time telling early on which of you is the real one.

If you are the Bard, you can choose only Townsfolk who have already used their abilities. That checks whether they are Townsfolk without making an important Townsfolk drunk.

If you are the Bard, you can choose only Outsiders: if you learn that some of them are Townsfolk, your information must be wrong.

If you are the Bard, don't choose yourself: if you are drunk, your information means nothing.

If you are the Bard, think carefully before choosing lots of players. Making many Townsfolk drunk may not be good for the good team, and it is hard to tell from a crowd which players are Townsfolk and which aren't.
bard.bluffing:
If you are a Minion ready to charge in, you can boldly choose the important Townsfolk in public. If they don't execute you, then when they later share their information, you can argue that it came while they were drunk and can't be trusted.

If you are the Demon, choose carefully and report believable information. This will help you survive into the late game.

You can claim to be the Bard for the first few days and switch to another character once the bluff fails. Claiming the Bard to help the real Bard hide is something good players often do.

aerialist.ability: On the night you die, you learn 1 player of each character type. If you die by execution after a good player nominated you, or by a good player's ability, you are drunk.
aerialist.summary: When the Aerialist dies, they learn players of different character types.
aerialist.examples:
Player 1 (the Demon) nominates and executes the Aerialist. That night the Aerialist is woken and learns player 1 (Demon), player 2 (Minion), player 3 (Outsider) and player 4 (Townsfolk).

Player 1 (a good Townsfolk) nominates and executes the Aerialist, so the Aerialist is drunk. That night the Aerialist is woken and learns player 1 (Townsfolk), player 2 (Townsfolk), player 3 (Outsider) and player 4 (Townsfolk).

There are no Outsiders in play. On the second night the Demon kills the Aerialist, who is woken that night and learns one Demon player, one Minion player and one Townsfolk player.

On the second night the Lycanthrope kills the Aerialist, so the Aerialist is drunk. That night the Aerialist is woken and learns 4 Townsfolk players.
aerialist.tips:
If you are the Aerialist, bluff an important Townsfolk to tempt the Demon into killing you at night.

If you are the Aerialist and the group doesn't know whom to execute, or you are about to be executed, reveal your character before nominations and pick a player you think is evil: ask them to nominate and execute you. Most players will back this, and good players will happily execute you. If they refuse, they are very likely evil.

If you are the Aerialist, don't reveal your character; deliberately bait or provoke a player you think is evil into nominating and executing you. Catch them off guard.

If you are the Aerialist and you got your information through an execution, think hard about whether it is true or false.

If you are the Aerialist and you got your information by dying at night, it is very likely true.

If you are the Aerialist, analyse your information carefully and share it with everyone. Find the player most likely to be the Demon and try to execute them.

If you are the Aerialist and the Vortox is in play, your information will be false; its only value is that it is certainly not true. Think it over — perhaps the Storyteller has ruled out a key possibility for you!
aerialist.bluffing:
The Aerialist works as a backup bluff: when a bluff as some other important Townsfolk fails, you can claim that you are really the Aerialist and were misleading evil to get the Demon to kill you, to help the good team.

If you are a less important Minion, you can reveal that you are the Aerialist and ask a player (someone else, or a teammate) to nominate and execute you. Then use your "information" to attack other players or protect your teammates.

truelove.ability: On your 1st day, you may invite the Storyteller to witness you & a player telling each other your characters. Then you privately learn if anyone lied.
truelove.summary: The Truelove can learn whether another player lied.
truelove.examples:
On the first day, the Truelove invites the Storyteller into a small room to witness them and the Goblin player telling each other their characters. The Truelove says they are the Truelove; the Goblin player says they are the Shugenja. After the Goblin player leaves, the Storyteller tells the Truelove "someone lied".

On the first day, the Vortox is in play. The Truelove invites the Storyteller to witness them and the Vortox player telling each other their characters. In front of all the players, the Truelove says they are the Truelove and the Vortox player says they are the Shugenja. The Storyteller then quietly whispers to the Truelove: "nobody lied".

On the first day, the Goblin player invites the Storyteller to witness them and the Shugenja player telling each other their characters. In front of all the players, the Goblin player says they are the Truelove and the Shugenja player says they are the Shugenja. The Storyteller then pretends to whisper something to the Goblin, but actually says nothing.
truelove.tips:
If you are the Truelove, announce on the first day that you are the Truelove and pick a suitable player to use your ability on. Everyone needs your information to make a first guess at which Demon is in play.

If you are the Truelove, among the players willing to go with you, pick the ones with the weightier characters: confirming their characters matters more to the game.

If you are the Truelove, tell the other player clearly that they are taking part in your ability and get their agreement. Otherwise, if they refuse to cooperate after you invite the Storyteller over, you have wasted your ability.

If you are the Truelove and you learn "someone lied", think hard about what went wrong: did the other player deceive you, is the Demon the Vortox, or are you the Drunk?

If you are the Truelove and you learn "nobody lied", in most cases you can trust that the player who swapped characters with you is who they said.

If you are the Truelove: the Truelove detects whether a player lied. A player who thinks they are one character but is actually the Drunk or the Doll counts as not lying as long as they tell you the character they believe they are, so you can't expose the Drunk or the Doll.

If you are evil, be careful about accepting the Truelove's invitation. If the Truelove learns that you lied, you immediately come under suspicion.

If you are evil and you know the Truelove is poisoned or drunk, or a character like the Vortox is in play, you can swap characters with the Truelove without worry.
truelove.bluffing:
If you are a Minion, you can claim to be the Truelove and get as many players as possible to tell you their characters. This gives you more information, which you can try to pass to the Demon so they kill the more important players first.

If you are the Goblin or the Baron, you can be more aggressive and tell everyone someone lied. That lets you attack the player who swapped characters with you, or else makes everyone think the Demon in play is the Vortox. Of course, this raises your risk of being executed.

If you are the Demon or the Scarlet Woman, you can protect yourself more carefully: tell everyone nobody lied, so that they accept and trust you.

ronin.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a player: if the Demon attacks them tonight, an evil player is attacked instead, and you regain this ability.
ronin.summary: The Ronin can turn the Demon's attack back on the evil team.
ronin.examples:
On the second night, the Ronin is woken and chooses the Noble, and the Demon also chooses the Noble. In the morning the Storyteller announces that the Widow died (the Widow was attacked instead). The next night the Ronin is woken again (their ability is regained).

On the fourth night, the only evil player still alive is the Demon. That night the Ronin is woken and chooses the Fool, who still has their ability, and the Demon also chooses the Fool. In the morning the Storyteller announces that the Demon died: the game ends and good wins. (The Demon attacked themself.)

On the second night, the Ronin is woken and chooses the Noble, and the Demon chooses the Seamstress. In the morning the Storyteller announces that the Seamstress died. The Ronin is not woken again for the rest of the game.
ronin.tips:
If you are the Ronin, try to read the Demon's mind: whom will they choose? You only get one chance, so use your ability on the night you think it is most likely to succeed.

If you are the Ronin: each time your ability succeeds, there is one fewer evil player. That is a huge disadvantage for evil. If it succeeds twice, evil's chances are slim. If it succeeds three times, you will have killed the Demon outright.

If you are the Ronin and you used your ability but were still woken the next night, your ability succeeded the night before, and whoever died that night was certainly evil.

If you are the Ronin and you used your ability last night but are not woken tonight, your ability did not succeed: the Demon did not attack the player you protected.

If you are the Ronin, don't rush to use your ability. Wait until a key Townsfolk has revealed their character, then protect them: your chance of success goes up a lot.

If you are the Ronin, bluffing an important Townsfolk and then protecting yourself is also a good strategy.

If you are the Ronin and the player you protected died that very night, you may be the Drunk, or poisoned or drunk. Think it over.

If you are the Demon, be careful about attacking an important Townsfolk on the night right after they reveal their character: that is exactly when the Ronin tends to protect them.

If you are the Demon and yesterday's dead player was not the one you chose but one of your Minions, it was most likely the Ronin's work. They may well use their ability again tonight, so avoid whomever they are protecting. If the Ronin succeeds twice, evil often collapses.
ronin.bluffing:
You can claim to have protected an important player; this makes you look fairly believable.

If you claim you were woken on the night after using your ability, you are accusing whoever died the night before of being evil. They may call you an evil player in disguise because you attacked them.

You can also claim that the player you protected last night died anyway, to pass yourself off as the Drunk, or as poisoned or drunk.

After a Minion claims to be the Goblin, you can have the Demon kill them at night, then claim you protected an important player. The Minion's death then looks like your doing, which wins you most players' trust.

lunar_knight.ability: Each night*, if nobody died by execution today, you are woken to choose a player: if they are a Minion, they die.
lunar_knight.summary: The Lunar Knight hunts Minions on nights after nobody died by execution.
lunar_knight.examples:
On the first day, the Psychopath is executed but does not die. That night, the Lunar Knight is woken and chooses the Psychopath, who dies.

On the first day, the Baron dies by execution. That night, the Lunar Knight is not woken.
lunar_knight.tips:
If you are the Lunar Knight, do your best to persuade everyone to execute the players on either side of the Tea Lady! Executing the Fool, or not executing anyone, also gets you woken. Trigger your ability as often as you can, and hunt down the suspected Minions!

If you are the Lunar Knight: you act very early in the night — even before the Demon! Apart from the Narcotizer, you have little to fear!

If you are the Lunar Knight and the player you chose died, come forward as the Lunar Knight quickly and claim your glory! Everyone will tend to see you as the hero who killed a Minion.

If you are the Lunar Knight and the player you chose did not die, don't lose heart: the player you chose is not a Minion! Tell everyone — it is an important clue. If you are all sure they are evil, then not being a Minion, they are very likely the Demon.

If you are the Demon: the Lunar Knight is a maximum threat to Minions. Making sure a player dies by execution every day is the best way to stop the Lunar Knight from acting. If several Townsfolk in play can make an execution fail to kill, you have to decide whether to kill them first or the Lunar Knight first.

If you are a Minion and you can't stop the Lunar Knight from acting, try hard not to look like a Minion! Otherwise you may well die on the Lunar Knight's lance.
lunar_knight.bluffing:
If several players die in the night, coming forward as the Lunar Knight and claiming one of them as your kill is fairly believable. But doing so will almost certainly draw a counter-attack from that player, since they are not a Minion! Be ready to face them.

If the Demon is the Cerberus, you are well suited to bluff the Lunar Knight, because the Cerberus itself can cause several deaths by killing Minions. Claiming that the dead Minion was your kill is easier to believe — because they really were a Minion! And as your teammate, they won't react badly; they may even help you pass as the Lunar Knight.

If you bluff the Lunar Knight, do what a Lunar Knight would do! For example, push to execute the players on either side of the Tea Lady, or the Fool, or propose not executing anyone.

lady_of_the_lake.ability: Each night, the Storyteller shows you 2 abilities. You may choose 1: it replaces your ability.
lady_of_the_lake.summary: The Lady of the Lake gets to pick their own ability.
lady_of_the_lake.examples:
On the first night, the Storyteller shows the Lady of the Lake 2 abilities, "You can't die at night" and "Your neighbours can't be poisoned or drunk", and the Lady of the Lake chooses the first. On later nights, the Lady of the Lake is not woken again.

On the first night, the Storyteller shows the Lady of the Lake the Seamstress's ability and the Washerwoman's ability, and the Lady of the Lake shakes their head. On the second night, the Storyteller shows the Soldier's ability and the Slayer's ability, and the Lady of the Lake chooses the Slayer's. The next day, the Lady of the Lake uses the Slayer's ability and kills the Demon.
lady_of_the_lake.tips:
If you are the Lady of the Lake: each night you have 2 options. If one of them suits the moment, pick it and use it quickly!

If you are the Lady of the Lake and no suitable ability comes up, you can keep waiting. Perhaps the Storyteller will offer something you like the next night.

If you are the Lady of the Lake, you don't have to tell anyone what your ability actually is, which leaves the evil team unsure how to deal with it.

If you are the Demon, try to find out what the Lady of the Lake's ability is, so that you can pick the best way to handle it.
lady_of_the_lake.bluffing:
Make up an ability that explains your actions, so that what you did earlier looks more reasonable.

Bluff the Lady of the Lake and ask other players to do something that helps you, explaining that it is what your ability needs to work.

paperboy.ability: Each day, you may get a news story from the Storyteller. If you read it out publicly, that night you learn if it is true.
paperboy.summary: Each day, the Paperboy brings all sorts of news from around town.
paperboy.examples:
On the first day, the Paperboy visits the Storyteller and learns: "Shock! Best friends Ducky and Lemon are secretly on opposite teams!" They read the story out publicly. That night, the Storyteller wakes them and they learn "yes".

On the first day, the Paperboy visits the Storyteller and learns: "The Scarlet Woman and the Baron were both seen in town." They don't read it out that day, and that night the Storyteller does not wake them.
paperboy.tips:
If you are the Paperboy, you can read out several news stories each day (the one you really got plus some you made up), so that the Demon can't tell what information you are about to have, which muddles their decision on whether to kill you.

If you are not the Paperboy — say you are the Sage or the Ronin — you can still read out news during the day to cover for the real Paperboy. If the Demon mistakes you for the real Paperboy and kills you, your own ability gets to work.

If you are the Demon: in general, a player who read no news during the day is certainly not the Paperboy, and a player who did is not necessarily the Paperboy. Decide whether to attack a Paperboy based on how important the "news" is.
paperboy.bluffing:
From the first day, dutifully read out your information in public and pose as a hard-working Paperboy. Keep your news weak, so that it doesn't seem very important: that explains why you never die at night.

Stick as closely as you can to the style of real news items, and avoid inventing anything too outlandish, or other players will see at a glance that you are lying.

If your Paperboy bluff fails, you can go on to claim to be the Sage, the Ronin, the Silversmith or the Aerialist, and explain that you were bluffing to help the good team mislead the Demon.

tuner.ability: You start knowing an Outsider character & a Minion character. Exactly 1 of them is in play.
tuner.summary: The Tuner learns about Outsider and Minion characters.
tuner.examples:
On the first night, the Tuner learns the Drunk and the Baron. In this game, the Drunk is in play and the Baron is not.

On the first night, the Tuner learns the Ogre and the Scarlet Woman. In this game, the Ogre is not in play and the Scarlet Woman is.

On the first night, the Tuner learns the Ogre and the Goblin. The Vortox is in play. In this game, neither the Ogre nor the Goblin is in play (false information).

On the first night, the Tuner learns the Drunk and the Baron. The Vortox is in play. In this game, both the Drunk and the Baron are in play (false information).
tuner.tips:
You can reveal your character and information early, so that everyone has a basic picture of the game.

You can also hide your character and reveal it, with your information, once the game has moved on. First, the Demon may take you for a more important Townsfolk and kill you at night — when you already have all your information — helping more important Townsfolk survive longer. Second, evil doesn't know what you learned, and may misread the game (for example, your information may make it fairly clear that the Baron is not in play while evil is bluffing several Outsiders).

The Vortox interferes with your information. If you can be sure the Demon in play is the Vortox, then the 2 characters you learned are either both in play or both not in play.
tuner.bluffing:
Reveal your character and information early so that people are as likely as possible to believe you.

Keep the Tuner as a backup bluff: when your first bluff is exposed, you can say you are really the Tuner and were only posing as a more important Townsfolk to mislead the Demon.

If the Baron is not in play, you can report a Minion other than the Baron plus an Outsider that is obviously in play (say the Snitch — Minions know whether the Snitch is in play). This helps evil fake a game where the Baron is in play.

Or, to fake another Minion being in play, report that Minion plus an Outsider that is obviously not in play.

Whatever you report, remember that the Vortox affects the Tuner's information. If everyone becomes sure the Demon in play is the Vortox and your information can't be explained, you may be executed.

perfumer.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a player or an evil character: they learn that the Perfumer is in play.
perfumer.summary: The Perfumer can prove themself or attack other players in different ways.
perfumer.examples:
On the first night, the Perfumer chooses player 1, and player 1 learns that the Perfumer is in play.

On the first night, the Perfumer chooses the Goblin. The Goblin is player 1, and player 1 learns that the Perfumer is in play.

On the first night, the Perfumer chooses the Goblin. The Goblin is not in play, so nobody learns that the Perfumer is in play.
perfumer.tips:
Don't go looking for the player you chose; wait for them to announce that the Perfumer is in play. An evil player who learns the Perfumer is in play can't tell whether you chose a player or an evil character, so they usually don't dare to speak up (a guilty conscience). If you go to them first, they can be almost sure you chose a player, and can then say without worry that they learned the Perfumer is in play.

Use your ability on a player you trust: once they announce that the Perfumer is in play, they vouch for you being the Perfumer.

Use your ability on a player you don't trust: if they never mention that the Perfumer is in play, they are very likely an evil player with a guilty conscience.

Choose an evil character and wait for a bite. If a player claims they learned the Perfumer is in play, you can be almost sure they are the evil character you chose.
perfumer.bluffing:
If you are a Minion that doesn't fear death much, like the Baron or the Goblin, you can claim you chose a player who then denies learning that the Perfumer is in play. You can then attack them as a guilty evil player and steer everyone into executing them.

You can put on a double act with an evil teammate: one of you claims to be the Perfumer and the other claims to have learned the Perfumer is in play, so that you confirm each other as good.

If you have a Goblin teammate, have them claim first that they learned the Perfumer is in play. Then say that you are the Perfumer and chose some Demon or the Scarlet Woman, staging a successful catch. This steers everyone into executing the Goblin, and even if the Goblin then claims to be the Goblin, everyone will think they are just a non-Goblin player struggling in their last moments.

martyra.ability: If a Minion dies by execution, you die that night, and all evil characters are drunk until dusk tomorrow.
martyra.summary: The Martyra dies on the night after a Minion is executed.
martyra.examples:
The Mastermind dies by execution, and that night the Martyra dies because of her own ability. The Vortox chooses the Seamstress that night; the Seamstress doesn't die and gets true information, because the Demon is drunk. In the morning, the Storyteller announces that the Martyra died.

The Vortox is in play. A Townsfolk dies by execution; that night the Vortox kills the Martyra, and the Seamstress gets false information.

A Minion dies by execution. That night the Innkeeper protects the Martyra, so the Martyra doesn't die. Since the Martyra didn't die, the Demon's and Minions' abilities work normally that night.
martyra.tips:
If you did not die in the night, the player executed that day was not a Minion.

If you die at night — especially if you are the only one who dies — think carefully about whether you died because of your own ability or for some other reason. If you died because of your own ability, the Townsfolk's information that night is highly reliable, since Minion and Demon interference is ruled out.

If you are still alive in the middle or late game, be wary: either all the Minions are still alive, or you were poisoned or drunk at some point.
martyra.bluffing: The Martyra is a hard character to bluff: if you don't die at night, it is hard to explain why.

cowboy.ability: On the 1st night, a Minion learns that the Cowboy is in play. Each time they nominate, you are woken that night. Whichever of you is first nominated by the other is executed immediately.
cowboy.summary: The Cowboy duels with their nemesis.
cowboy.examples:
On the first night, the Poisoner learns that the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Cowboy nominates the Poisoner, who is executed immediately and dies. The Storyteller declares nightfall.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns that the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Storyteller opens nominations, and the Cowboy and the Poisoner nominate each other at the same moment. The Storyteller hears the Poisoner's nomination first, so the Cowboy is executed immediately and dies. The Storyteller declares nightfall.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns that the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Poisoner nominates a player. That night, the Cowboy is woken.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns that the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Poisoner does not nominate. On the second night, the Cowboy is not woken. On the second day, the Cowboy nominates the Imp, and then the Poisoner nominates the Cowboy: the Cowboy is executed immediately and dies. The Storyteller declares nightfall.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns that the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, another player nominates the Poisoner, who dies by execution; that night the Cowboy is not woken. On the second day, the Cowboy nominates the dead Poisoner, who is executed immediately. The Storyteller declares nightfall.

On the first night, the Poisoner learns that the Cowboy is in play. On the first day, the Cowboy is poisoned and nominates the Poisoner; the nomination proceeds normally. The next day, the Cowboy is healthy again and the Poisoner nominates the Cowboy; the nomination proceeds normally (the Cowboy's ability was wasted while poisoned).
cowboy.tips:
Revealing that you are the Cowboy early in the game is very dangerous: your nemesis may beat you to the nomination. That isn't necessarily bad — it at least proves that one of you is the Cowboy and the other a Minion — but it is better if the one lying on the floor is the Minion.

Ignore players you have already nominated, or who have nominated you: they are not your nemesis (as long as you weren't poisoned or drunk).

You can make a seemingly casual nomination every day. Perhaps luck is on your side and you hit your nemesis on the first try?

You can also avoid nominating early on, though that makes it easy for your nemesis to guess you are the Cowboy. After gathering a few nights of information, strike precisely and finish them in one blow.

If you are the Minion who learned the Cowboy is in play (the nemesis), find out quickly who the Cowboy is and watch whether the Cowboy has marked you as the nemesis before you act.

If you are the Minion who learned the Cowboy is in play (the nemesis), the best way to handle the Cowboy may be to ask your Demon boss to kill them at night, or to nominate them — or get them to nominate you — while they are poisoned. Even if you execute them through a nomination, it proves that one of you is the Cowboy and the other a Minion; unless you publicly claim to be the Cowboy yourself, everyone will see you as the Minion.

If you are the Minion who learned the Cowboy is in play (the nemesis) and the Cowboy has revealed themself, you can claim to be the Cowboy too. You are then locked in a fight to the death that day. With enough luck, you not only beat them but also convince everyone that you are the real Cowboy.
cowboy.bluffing:
The Cowboy is a hard character to bluff. If you never trigger your ability to execute a player, or get executed, all game, it is hard to make other players believe you are the Cowboy.

If you bluff the Cowboy and survive into the late game, think ahead about how to explain to the others why your ability never fired. Usually "my nemesis is already dead" is a fairly reasonable explanation, but other players may still ask you to nominate dead players to try to trigger an execution and prove you are the Cowboy.

the_cat_adventurers.ability: Each day, a player who has never adventured may publicly volunteer to adventure. That night, if they are alive, you learn a player of the opposite alignment to them.
the_cat_adventurers.summary: Each day, The Cat Adventurers send out an adventurer to find a player of another alignment.
the_cat_adventurers.examples:
On the first day, the Noble publicly announces "I'm going adventuring!" That night the Demon does not kill the Noble, and The Cat Adventurers learn the Poisoner player. On the second day, the Noble announces "I'm going adventuring!" again; since the Noble has already adventured, the Storyteller refuses.

On the first day, the Noble publicly announces "I'm joining the glorious Cat Adventurers!" That night the Demon kills the Noble, and The Cat Adventurers are not woken.

On the first day, the Noble publicly announces "I'm The Cat Adventurers' vanguard guide!" That night the CodeX kills The Cat Adventurers, who are not woken.

On the first day, the Poisoner publicly announces "I'll defend the honour of The Cat Adventurers to the death!" That night the Demon does not kill the Poisoner, and The Cat Adventurers learn the Noble player.

On the first day, the Noble publicly announces "I'll be The Cat Adventurers' guide!", then the Poisoner announces "I'll clear the way for The Cat Adventurers!" The Noble got in first, so the Storyteller turns the Poisoner down.

On the first day, The Cat Adventurers are not in play. The Noble publicly announces "I'm The Cat Adventurers' vanguard guide!", and the Storyteller answers "Noted" just as if The Cat Adventurers were in play.
the_cat_adventurers.tips:
Encourage people to go adventuring! Otherwise you do nothing at all. If it comes to it, you can go yourself!

The adventurer and the player you learn that night are of different alignments, but the adventurer isn't necessarily good, and the player you learn isn't necessarily evil. Evil players volunteering to adventure is very common.

If you think the adventurer and the player you learned are on the same team, consider whether the Vortox is in play or you are poisoned or drunk.

If you are a good character who doesn't fear death, try to go adventuring! If you survive, The Cat Adventurers can learn a player of the other alignment to you. Even if you die, you took a hit for another important Townsfolk! If you are a character who wants to die at night, like the Aerialist, all the more reason to volunteer.

If you are a good character who does fear death, adventuring puts you at great risk of dying. But you can still adventure: bluff that you are a character who doesn't fear death, or even one like the Aerialist who wants to die at night. If you fool the Demon, you get through the night safely.

If you are an evil player, you can also volunteer! Most people see volunteering as playing actively. And if you adventure, The Cat Adventurers certainly won't learn the Demon or another important teammate of yours that day.

If you are the Demon and think The Cat Adventurers may be in play, think carefully about your next move. Kill that day's adventurer, to make sure The Cat Adventurers learn nothing that day? Gamble on killing the player you suspect is The Cat Adventurers? Or let it be? Killing the adventurer guarantees The Cat Adventurers get nothing that day, but it may only put off the problem, since a new adventurer will appear tomorrow.
the_cat_adventurers.bluffing:
Take care when bluffing The Cat Adventurers! If the adventurer dies that day, or there is no adventurer that day, you are not woken.

Offer opinions every day on who should go adventuring: it helps people believe you are The Cat Adventurers.

Think carefully about how to report your information. It sets 2 players against each other, and if they are inclined to believe each other good, they may team up against you. Usually, naming a player whom that day's adventurer already distrusted helps you win the others' trust.

ranger.ability: If one of your alive neighbours dies, you are woken that night to choose a player: if they are a Minion, they die.
ranger.summary: The Ranger hunts Minions on the night a player next to them dies.
ranger.examples:
The Paperboy is the Ranger's nearest alive player. During the day the Paperboy dies by execution; that night the Ranger is woken and chooses the Widow, who dies.

The Paperboy is the Ranger's nearest alive player. At night the Demon kills the Paperboy; that night the Ranger is woken and chooses the Widow, who dies.

The Ranger sits next to the Paperboy. During the day the Paperboy dies by execution; that night the Ranger is woken and chooses the Vortox. Nothing happens.

The Ranger sits next to the Paperboy, who is already dead and is executed again during the day. That night the Ranger is not woken.
ranger.tips:
Find a way to get your nearest alive players killed. Only when they die are you woken to use your ability.

If your neighbours are important Townsfolk, they will likely die at night anyway. No need to hurry — just wait for their deaths.

If the player you choose doesn't die, they are certainly not a Minion. If you are sure they are evil, they are very likely the Demon.
ranger.bluffing:
Pushing to execute your neighbours makes you look more like a Ranger.

If one of your neighbours dies that day, remember that as the Ranger you would be woken to act. Decide in advance which choice you will say you made.

valkyrie.ability: Each night*, deaths are delayed until you approve the list of deaths. If you don't approve it, only you die tonight.
valkyrie.summary: The Valkyrie can choose to sacrifice herself to protect other players.
valkyrie.examples:
On the second night, the CodeX kills the Noble and the Demon kills the Sweetheart, but the Valkyrie's ability delays their deaths, so the Sweetheart's ability does not trigger yet. The Valkyrie is woken and the Storyteller points to the Noble player and the Sweetheart player. The Valkyrie nods to agree: the Noble and the Sweetheart die, and a player becomes drunk.

On the second night, the CodeX kills the Sweetheart and the Demon kills the Valkyrie, but the Valkyrie's ability delays their deaths, so the Sweetheart's ability does not trigger yet. The Valkyrie is woken and the Storyteller points to the Valkyrie player and the Sweetheart player. The Valkyrie shakes her head to refuse: the Valkyrie dies and the Sweetheart doesn't.

On the second night, the Demon kills themself, but the Valkyrie's ability delays their death. The Valkyrie is woken and the Storyteller points to the Demon player. The Valkyrie shakes her head to refuse: the Valkyrie dies and the Demon doesn't.

On the second night, the Demon kills themself, but the Valkyrie's ability delays their death. The Valkyrie is woken and the Storyteller points to the Demon player. The Valkyrie nods to agree: the only alive Demon dies and the game ends.
valkyrie.tips:
Your ability is extraordinarily strong: if you don't want certain players to die at night, they won't! Quietly protect the players you think matter. Don't use your ability lightly before they are on the list of deaths.

If you see your own name on the list of deaths, you had better use your ability. Either way, you most likely won't survive the night, and you may save some of the other players dying with you.

If you see 2, 3 or even more players on the list of deaths, think carefully about using your ability. Trading your life for more players' lives is usually a good deal.

After using your ability, tell everyone whom you protected. Players who would die at night are usually good.

Beware of cunning evil players tricking you into using your ability! Minions, or even the Demon, may kill themselves to trick you into protecting them!

If you are evil, spread out the evil team's killing abilities carefully! Causing too many deaths in one go is easily undone by the Valkyrie's ability!

If you are the Demon, you could try an evil plan: kill other evil players, or even yourself, to trick the Valkyrie into protecting you! It is of course very high risk — but the bigger the risk, the bigger the reward! If the Valkyrie protects you, you are certainly a good player in her eyes.
valkyrie.bluffing:
The Valkyrie is a hard character for the Demon to bluff. After an important Townsfolk dies, people will often ask why you didn't step in to protect them. If you can't give a good answer, you may be executed.

Having a Minion bluff the Valkyrie and then get killed by the Demon at night is a good plan. The dead Minion can claim to have protected the Demon or another evil player, making them look more like a good player.

hanged_man.ability: When the game ends, if you ever voted with a vote token, the winning & losing teams are swapped.
hanged_man.summary: After dying, the Hanged Man can reverse the result of the game.
hanged_man.examples:
The only Demon dies by execution: the game ends and good wins. Because the Hanged Man voted with their vote token that day, the result is swapped and evil wins.

A player dies by execution, leaving 2 alive players including the Demon: the game ends and evil wins. Because the Hanged Man voted with their vote token earlier, the result is swapped and good wins.

The only Demon kills themself: the game ends and good wins. Because the Hanged Man voted with their vote token earlier, the result is swapped and evil wins.
hanged_man.tips:
If you are the Hanged Man, it is best not to reveal your real character lightly. If evil learns you are the Hanged Man, they can plan their votes and kills around whether you have used your vote token.

If you are the Hanged Man, you don't fear death — you even need to seek it, since you only have an ability once you are dead. You can bluff an important character and hope the Demon kills you at night. That gets you killed without wasting an execution.

If you are the Hanged Man and the player you think is the Demon is about to be executed, don't vote with your vote token, or you may well do more harm than good.

If you are the Hanged Man and you have already spent your vote token, your job from then on is to "make evil win" by any means, such as rallying everyone to execute the remaining good players. But don't make it too obvious: once the Demon knows your ability has triggered, they may kill themself to end the game.

If you are a good player, you can claim to be the Hanged Man after you die and spend your vote token. If you act well enough, the Demon may be fooled into killing themself.

If you are the Demon: until a good player has used a vote token, no Hanged Man's ability can have triggered. Don't worry too much about the Hanged Man.

If you are the Demon and you think the Hanged Man may be in play, find out quickly who it is and keep a close eye on their death and their votes. If they use their vote token, "kill yourself" as soon as you can, by execution or otherwise.

If you are the Demon, there are only 4 alive players including you, and you believe the Hanged Man has used their vote token, find a way to get yourself executed. If they execute someone else, kill yourself after nightfall: the Hanged Man's ability then lets you win immediately.

If you are the Demon, there are only 3 alive players including you, and you believe the Hanged Man has used their vote token, do everything you can to die by execution today. If they execute the other alive player instead, you immediately "win" because only 2 players are alive — but since the Hanged Man's ability has triggered, you lose.
hanged_man.bluffing:
If you are a Minion, you can bluff the Hanged Man after you die. On the final day, urge everyone to execute a good player, to "trigger the Hanged Man's ability". Of course there is no Hanged Man, so you win because the Demon survives to the end.

If you realise that the Hanged Man's ability has already triggered and the game is heading out of your control, you can claim that you are the real Hanged Man, that your ability never triggered, and that the result won't be swapped. Use this to steer players into executing whomever you want executed.

The Hanged Man makes a good backup bluff after another bluff fails. The Hanged Man usually doesn't reveal their character, so it is a fairly workable plan. In the middle or late game, especially on the final day, you can claim to be the Hanged Man after all and steer players into executing the wrong player.

joker.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself): you learn their suit. The 4 suits secretly match the 4 character types.
joker.summary: The Joker can see other players' card suits, but has to crack what the suits mean.
joker.examples:
On the first night, the Joker chooses the Imp and learns diamonds. On the second night, the Joker chooses the Exorcist and learns spades. On the third night, the Joker chooses the Washerwoman and learns spades. For this Joker in this game, spades are Townsfolk, hearts are Outsiders, clubs are Minions and diamonds are the Demon.

On the first night, the Joker chooses the Saint and learns hearts. On the second night, the Joker chooses the Butler and learns hearts. On the third night, the Joker chooses the Widow and learns spades. On the fourth night, the Joker chooses the Baron and learns spades. For this Joker in this game, spades are Minions, hearts are Outsiders, clubs are the Demon and diamonds are Townsfolk.
joker.tips:
Do whatever you can to work out what each of your 4 suits means, whether by discussing it with everyone or by checking it against other players' information.

If 2 players have different suits but both claim to be Townsfolk, at least one of them is not a Townsfolk — maybe both!

If you have already learned all 4 suits, one of those players is certainly the Demon!

If you have checked 2 players who claim to be Townsfolk and they share a suit, be extremely wary of any later player who claims to be a Townsfolk but shows a different suit! They are very likely not Townsfolk. There is, of course, a tiny chance that the 2 players you checked earlier are both Minions, which would also give them the same suit.

One night of information is useless on its own, so do whatever it takes to survive past the second night.

Early on your information is worth little or nothing, but it becomes more valuable over time. If you live into the middle or late game and have cracked your suits, your information can be decisive. Staying alive is your first goal.

If you are evil, you can bluff an Outsider and steer the Joker into choosing you. That will make it much harder for them to sort out their information.

If you are the Demon, the Joker is your top target. The longer the Joker lives, the more dangerous their information becomes; once they have it worked out, it helps good enormously. You don't want the Joker alive at the end — deal with them quickly.
joker.bluffing:
Before you build your story, talk to the players who seem good first and quietly gather the characters they claim, publicly or privately. Use this to construct your narrative so that your "information" fits neatly into the existing claims, which makes it far more believable.

Watch the chains of trust within the good team closely. A clever move is to aim your "checks" at players who are already wary of each other. For example, if you notice someone strongly doubting another player's claim, put both of them in your "information". This sharpens their existing conflict and pushes them into mutual accusations, buying you room to survive.

Whatever you do, don't rush to publish your "information" early in the game. At the start you know next to nothing, and the more you say, the more mistakes you make. The hardest part of this bluff is the opening. Watch the game for a few days, and once the claims in play are clearer, release your carefully prepared "information" bit by bit. Being right is not the main thing; what matters is that it fits the current state of the game and sounds reasonable.

mummy.ability: If you die by execution after an evil player nominated you, or by an evil player's ability, you are resurrected when Judgment Day arrives.
mummy.summary: If the Mummy dies at the hands of an evil player, they are resurrected on Judgment Day.
mummy.examples:
On the first day, the Mummy dies after being nominated by the Demon. On Judgment Day, the Storyteller announces that the Mummy is resurrected.

On the first day, the Mummy dies after being nominated by a good player. The Mummy's resurrection will not trigger this game.

On the second night, the Demon kills the Mummy. On Judgment Day, the Storyteller announces that the Mummy is resurrected.

On the second night, the Gossip kills the Mummy. The Mummy's resurrection will not trigger this game.
mummy.tips:
If you are the Mummy, your best fate is to die before Judgment Day arrives, by whatever means.

If you are the Mummy and you died by execution and were resurrected, the player who nominated you is certainly evil.

If you are the Mummy, you can hide your character and then come back to life on Judgment Day, which badly disrupts evil's plans.

If you are the Demon: the Mummy may give good an extra execution to work with. Watch out for it.

If you are the Demon, try not to attack or nominate the Mummy: as long as they stay alive, they do nothing.
mummy.bluffing:
The Mummy usually seeks out death, so if you want to bluff the Mummy, it is best to ask other players to nominate and execute you. That usually means a very high risk of dying.

You can use the fact that you were not resurrected on Judgment Day to "prove" that the player who nominated you is good.

skipper.ability: Each night*, you learn if the Demon is closer to the left or the right of today's executed player. If an evil player is executed, you are drunk until dawn.
skipper.summary: The Skipper narrows down the Demon, one execution at a time.
skipper.examples:
On the first day, a good player is executed. Between that player and the Demon, fewer players sit on the left than on the right. That night, the Skipper learns "left".

On the first day, an evil player is executed, so the Skipper is drunk. Between that player and the Demon, fewer players sit on the left than on the right. That night, the Skipper learns "right".

On the first day, a good player is executed. Between that player and the Demon, as many players sit on the left as on the right. That night, the Skipper learns "left".

On the third day, a good player is executed. There is a dead Demon and an alive Demon in play. The dead Demon is closer on the executed player's left, and the alive Demon is closer on their right. That night, the Skipper learns "right", because the Storyteller chose the alive Demon as the Demon the Skipper's ability locates.

On the third day, nobody is executed. That night, the Skipper is not woken.
skipper.tips:
If you are the Skipper, each piece of information lets you rule out roughly half the players as the Demon. Compare your results over several nights and look for the Demon among the players they point to again and again.

If you are the Skipper, you must "sacrifice" a good player for Poseidon to guide you; otherwise you are drunk and your information is meaningless. So if you believe the executed player was evil, that night's information is useless. Conversely, if your information is clearly off one night, the player executed that day is very likely evil.

If you are the Skipper and you keep executing players who sit next to each other, your information narrows things down very slowly. Executing players far from the previous executee each time helps you locate the Demon faster.

If you are the Demon, the Skipper's information is very strong: deal with them quickly. If you can't kill the Skipper yet, sending evil players to be executed also disrupts the Skipper's ability nicely.

If you are the Demon, push everyone to execute players next to the previous executee as much as you can; this makes the Skipper's information nearly worthless. Keep track of where you sit relative to each day's executee to avoid being found too quickly.
skipper.bluffing:
If you bluff the Skipper, make sure your information stays consistent. If your first result says "the Demon is on the left half" and your second says "the Demon is on the right half", your Skipper claim becomes far less believable.

Claim to be the Skipper and give opinions on whom to execute, saying that following your advice will find the Demon faster.

medium.ability: If a Townsfolk dies by execution after you nominated them, that night they learn that the Medium is in play.
medium.summary: Townsfolk learn when they have died at the Medium's hands.
medium.examples:
On the first day, the Medium nominates the Noble, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Noble is woken and learns that the Medium is in play.

On the second day, the Medium nominates the Butler, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Butler is not woken.

On the third day, the Medium nominates the Baron, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Baron is not woken.

On the fourth day, the Medium nominates the Fortune Teller, who dies by execution that day. That night, the Medium dies, and the Fortune Teller is not woken.
medium.tips:
If you are the Medium, try to nominate and execute other players, but preferably without revealing that you are the Medium. If a player you executed says they learned the Medium is in play, they are most likely a Townsfolk. If they deny it, they are most likely not a Townsfolk.

If you are the Medium, you can ask everyone to let you nominate, to prove you really are the Medium. But make sure the player you execute is a Townsfolk, or they won't learn the Medium is in play.

If you learn at night that the Medium is in play, you can be sure the player who nominated and executed you is the Medium. Don't make a fuss: talk to the Medium privately. The next time a Townsfolk player the Medium nominates and executes doesn't know about, or denies, the Medium being in play, the two of you can together establish that they are most likely evil!
medium.bluffing:
Bluff the Medium. Make a nomination and get the player executed; they will flatly deny learning the Medium is in play, and you attack them as evil.

Bluff the Medium. Nominate and execute your teammate, and cover for each other as the Medium and a Townsfolk.

miko.ability: Each night, choose 2 players (not yourself) who neighbour each other: you learn if either is a Minion.
miko.summary: The Miko can check players for Minions.
miko.examples:
On the first night, the Miko chooses the Fortune Teller and the Baron, who sit next to each other, and learns "yes".

On the second night, the Miko chooses the Saint and the Imp, who sit next to each other, and learns "no".
miko.tips:
If you are the Miko, your ability can quickly pin down or clear Minions. If you learn "no", neither player you chose is a Minion. If you learn "yes", at least one of them is a Minion.

If you are the Miko and you learn "yes", you can choose overlapping pairs again to work out exactly which player is the Minion.

If you are the Miko: your ability can't check for the Demon or other kinds of evil player, and a player you have cleared as not a Minion isn't necessarily good.

If you are a Minion and the Miko accuses you of being the Minion she found, she can't yet tell which of the pair it is. Use this to accuse your other neighbour of being the Minion.

If you are a Minion whose character isn't very important, stepping forward at the right moment to be "caught" and drawing everyone's attention is a very important technique — especially when the good team is focusing on the players around the Demon.
miko.bluffing:
Report that 2 players who are hostile to each other include a Minion, let them attack each other, and reap the rewards!

In the middle or late game, report that a pair including the Demon contains a Minion. Good may then take the Demon for a Minion and decide not to execute them. This is fairly risky, though.

Reporting players as not Minions can bring you closer to them. But if you never find a Minion, players will start to doubt your claim.

sensate.ability: Each night, the Demon chooses an alive player (not you): the Demon & you learn their character.
sensate.summary: The Sensate "shares sight" with the Demon, seeing what the Demon sees.
sensate.examples:
On the first night, the Demon uses the Sensate's ability to choose player 1 (the Sensate). The Storyteller shakes their head and has the Demon choose again, since the Sensate's ability can't choose the Sensate. The Demon chooses player 2 (the Chambermaid) and learns that player 2 is the Chambermaid. The Storyteller puts the Demon to sleep and wakes the Sensate, who learns that player 2 is the Chambermaid.

On the first night, the Demon uses the Sensate's ability to choose player 2 (the Chambermaid). The Demon learns that player 2 is the Chambermaid, and so does the Sensate. On the second night, player 2 is still alive. The Demon chooses player 2 (the Chambermaid) again; the Demon and the Sensate both learn that player 2 is the Chambermaid. On the third night, player 2 is dead. The Demon chooses player 2, and the Storyteller shakes their head, since the Sensate's ability can't choose dead players. The Demon chooses player 3 (the Fortune Teller); the Demon and the Sensate both learn that player 3 is the Fortune Teller.
sensate.tips:
If you are the Sensate, remember: whatever you learn, the Demon learns too! The player you see is the one the Demon chose to show you. So there is little point hiding your information, but some point hiding that you are the Sensate, so the Demon doesn't find and kill you too soon.

If you are the Sensate and a player claims to be the Sensate and correctly names other players' characters — especially if their information matches yours — they are evil. They may be the Demon, or a Minion sent by the Demon. Since they claim to be the Sensate, a head-to-head fight between the two of you is unavoidable.

If you are the Sensate, you can execute the player you learned to force the Demon to choose a new alive player, which gets you new information.

If you are the Sensate: usually the Demon will let you learn that a player is some good character. If you learn that a player is an evil character, think about why. Why would the Demon deliberately expose an evil player to you? Are you poisoned? Is the Demon the Vortox? Or is it a Demon plot to lure you into executing someone?

If you are the Demon, choosing the same alive player night after night limits the Sensate's information as much as possible and stops them learning a lot too quickly.

If you are the Demon and you choose an alive player but the Storyteller shakes their head and has you choose again, that player is the Sensate. You can kill them the next night if you need to.

If you are the Demon, choosing a Minion — or even the Demon — at the right moment will confuse the Sensate and throw off good's execution decisions. Only do this with a complete evil plan in mind.

If you are the Demon and the player you had been choosing has died, try to choose a player everyone already accepts as good. This keeps as many players as possible under suspicion of being evil.

If you are the Demon, you can send a Minion to claim to be the Sensate and privately confirm characters with the player you learned. This can win that player's trust for a while. But the real Sensate will come forward eventually, and the two Sensates will have to fight it out over who is real.
sensate.bluffing:
If the Demon was not woken for the Sensate's ability, there is no Sensate in play, and you can safely use the Sensate as an extra bluff.

The key to bluffing the Sensate is naming players' characters correctly, especially players who haven't revealed their characters. If you get one wrong, you may come under suspicion immediately.

To keep the Sensate from learning too much, in most cases the Demon chooses the same player for the first few days, unless that player has died. Remember that as the Sensate, you should always be learning the character of an alive player.

onmyoji.ability: Each night, you learn a player: they are the opposite alignment to the player you learned the previous night.
onmyoji.summary: The Onmyoji learns good and evil players in turn.
onmyoji.examples:
On the first night, the Onmyoji learns Alice. On the second night, Bob. On the third night, Carol. On the fourth night, Dave. Alice and Carol are good; Bob and Dave are evil.

On the first night, the Onmyoji learns Alice. On the second night, Bob. On the third night, Carol. On the fourth night, Dave. Alice and Carol are evil; Bob and Dave are good.
onmyoji.tips:
One night of information is useless on its own: that player could be good or evil. So do whatever it takes to survive past the second night.

If you have learned 2 players, exactly one of them is evil!
onmyoji.bluffing:
Report several good players and stir up conflict between them! Get them attacking each other!

Mix real evil players into your information: it makes you look more like a real Onmyoji.

druid.ability: If your 2 alive neighbours are the same alignment, the Demon can only attack them.
