If you are the Demon and lots of dead good players join the treasure hunt, they are wasting lots of vote tokens! Remember: the Pirate Cat King must be dead on Judgment Day for the ability to trigger! Just avoid the Pirate Cat King and let them live until Judgment Day, and those foolish good players lose their investment for good. Of course, they can choose to execute the Pirate Cat King before Judgment Day, but that surely gives you more chances to survive. If necessary, you can also have Minions become Treasure Hunters that day to get a share.

If you are evil and you can get the Pirate Cat King poisoned, removed from play, or ability-less on Judgment Day — anything at all, as long as their ability can't trigger normally — every Treasure Hunter loses everything! They lose their vote on the final day.
pirate_cat_king.bluffing:
Bluffing the Pirate Cat King and tricking lots of good players into giving up their vote tokens is a huge boon for evil! Those fools lose their vote on the final day!

If you bluff the Pirate Cat King, remember that people usually want the Pirate Cat King dead before the final day! That both gets the Treasure Hunters their vote tokens and proves you are the Pirate Cat King. So if you are the Demon, your risk of being executed is very high.

If you bluff the Pirate Cat King, remember that you have no real "treasure" to share. So even if you are dead when Judgment Day arrives, you can't prove on the final day that you are the Pirate Cat King. Unless you plan to reveal yourself as evil on Judgment Day, prepare an explanation in advance for why your ability didn't work.

gargoyle.ability: The 1st time another player nominates you, they die. If you kill an evil player, you become their character & alignment.
gargoyle.summary: The Gargoyle kills those who dare to offend them, but is easily won over by evil.
gargoyle.examples:
On the first day, the Fortune Teller nominates the Gargoyle. It is the first time another player has nominated the Gargoyle, so the Fortune Teller dies.

On the second day, the Poisoner nominates the Gargoyle. It is the first time another player has nominated the Gargoyle, so the Poisoner dies, and the Gargoyle becomes an evil Poisoner. That night, the Gargoyle is woken and learns that they have become an evil Poisoner.

On a day with only 3 alive players, the Imp nominates the Gargoyle. It is the first time another player has nominated the Gargoyle, so the Imp dies and the Gargoyle becomes an evil Imp. Only 2 players are alive: the game ends and evil wins.
gargoyle.tips:
If you are the Gargoyle and you don't want other players dropping dead to your ability, it is best to reveal that you are the Gargoyle and have other players be careful about nominating you. You can also nominate yourself first, to stop other players nominating you.

If you are the Gargoyle and your alignment and character haven't changed on the night after you kill a player, that player was good! You can announce this straight away in the morning. Of course, people may not believe you, since you would say the same even if you had turned evil!

If you are the Gargoyle and you have turned evil, the player you killed was certainly evil! You are no longer on the good team, and you have a new character and ability. Think hard about how best to serve evil!

If you are evil and you want to add a new recruit to the evil team, nominating the Gargoyle is a good choice. They will kill you, but they will inherit your character and ability and stay alive in play.

If you are the Demon and you think you are about to be exposed, nominate the Gargoyle and let them kill you and become the new Demon! It is one effective way to keep the Demon alive.

If you are a Minion and people think you may be the Demon, deliberately nominate the Gargoyle and let them kill you. People may then turn to executing the Gargoyle. You still die, but at least evil gains a teammate.
gargoyle.bluffing: Bluffing the Gargoyle is usually hard, since you don't have the Gargoyle's ability. But if the script has characters like the Yaggababble or the Witch that can help you pass as the Gargoyle, you can give it a try.

titan.ability: On the 1st night, you turn evil & gain the abilities of every not-in-play Minion. [The Titan counts as a Minion during setup]
titan.summary: The mighty Titan is an Outsider who joins the game in a Minion's place.
titan.examples:
A 9-player game with the Titan in play. The Titan replaced the only Minion, so no Minion is in play. On the first night, the Demon learns no Minions, since the Titan is an Outsider, not a Minion. The Titan turns evil and learns that they have the abilities of the Poisoner, Spy, Godfather and Devil's Advocate, and is woken to use each of them that night. The Titan gaining the Godfather's ability doesn't change the Outsider count, since that is a setup ability.

A 12-player game with the Titan in play. Only one Minion (the Godfather) is in play, because the Titan replaced a Minion. On the first night, the Demon learns that the Godfather player is a Minion, and the Godfather learns that the Imp player is the Demon. The Titan turns evil and learns that they have the abilities of the Mastermind, Pit-Hag and Assassin.

A 15-player game with the Titan in play. Only 2 Minions (the Godfather and the Assassin) are in play, because the Titan replaced a Minion. On the first night, the Demon learns that the Godfather and Assassin players are Minions, and the Godfather and Assassin learn that the Imp player is the Demon. The Titan turns evil and learns that they have the abilities of the Mastermind and the Pit-Hag.

On the third night, the Pit-Hag turns the Fortune Teller into the Titan. The new Titan doesn't turn evil and doesn't gain any Minion abilities, because the Titan's ability only triggers on the first night.
titan.tips:
If you are the Titan, think of yourself as an unusual Minion: you have powerful abilities, but you don't know who your teammates are. Use those abilities carefully and work out who your teammates are as quickly as you can.

If you are the Titan, you can use your own abilities to work out which Minions are in play, which helps you find who your teammates might be.

If you are the Titan, don't reveal to others that you are the Titan lightly: to good, the Titan is even scarier than a Minion, and they may be eager to execute you.

If you are good and it seems more Minion abilities are working than there should be Minions, the Titan is very likely in play!

If you are good: the Titan and their evil teammates can't recognise each other, so the game can get chaotic, with evil abilities hitting each other and even killing each other.

myconid.ability: You & the Minions keep your abilities after dying by execution.
myconid.summary: The Myconid and the Minions don't lose their abilities when executed.
myconid.examples:
On the first day, the Myconid is alive and the Witch dies by execution; the Witch keeps her ability. That night the Demon kills the Myconid, and the Witch loses her ability.

On the first day, the Myconid dies by execution and keeps their ability. On the second day, the Witch dies by execution and keeps her ability.

On the first day, the Myconid is alive and the Witch dies by execution; the Witch keeps her ability. On the second day, the Myconid dies by execution and keeps their ability, so the Witch still keeps hers. On the third day, the Assassin dies by execution and keeps their ability.
myconid.tips:
If you are the Myconid, try not to be executed: if you die by execution, Minions who are executed keep their abilities for the rest of the game!

If you are the Myconid and you die other than by execution, great! No Minion will keep their ability because of you from then on!

If you are the Myconid, you can hide as best you can, or bluff an important Townsfolk to tempt the Demon into killing you at night.

If you are a Minion and you are sure the Myconid is in play, you can let yourself be executed without worry, since you won't lose your ability.

If you are the Demon, be careful to avoid attacking the Myconid! Killing the Myconid makes Minions lose abilities they have kept, or stop keeping them when executed.
myconid.bluffing:
In the early and middle game, good usually doesn't want to execute a Myconid. But in the later game, the Myconid's ability won't save them from execution, since an alive Myconid and a Myconid who died by execution both let Minions keep their abilities.

In games with obvious signs of Minion abilities, the Myconid is an excellent bluff. You can argue that the Minion abilities persist because of your ability, and that the players who died by execution earlier included a Minion.

If you want to bluff the Myconid, don't reveal it in the early or middle game, because a real Myconid usually tries to pass as some other character early on.

The Myconid is a good backup bluff, since the ability gives Myconid players a reason to hide their real character. If your earlier bluff can't go on, just say you are the Myconid!

squid_girl.ability: The 1st time you would die, you might not die, but all Townsfolk are drunk until dusk tomorrow.
squid_girl.summary: When death threatens the Squid Girl, she makes players drunk.
squid_girl.examples:
On the first day, the Psychopath publicly chooses the Squid Girl. The Squid Girl doesn't die, and all Townsfolk become drunk.

On the first day, the Golem nominates the Squid Girl. The Squid Girl doesn't die, and all Townsfolk become drunk.

On the second night, the Imp chooses the Squid Girl. The Squid Girl doesn't die, and all Townsfolk become drunk.

On the first day, the Squid Girl is executed but doesn't die, and all Townsfolk become drunk. On the second day, the Squid Girl is executed and dies.
squid_girl.tips:
If you are the Squid Girl, you have an ability to escape death, but sadly it isn't guaranteed to trigger. If you should have died but didn't, your ability may have worked.

If you are the Squid Girl and you survive an execution, or a night is unusually quiet, you had better tell everyone you are the Squid Girl; otherwise you will badly mislead the other players.

If you are the Demon and you know who the Squid Girl is, attack her at the right moment to try to trigger her ability, which disrupts the Townsfolk's abilities.

If you are the Demon and you attack a player who doesn't die, she may be the Squid Girl! If she survived because of the Squid Girl's ability, all the Townsfolk are drunk.
squid_girl.bluffing:
If you have an ability that stops you dying by execution, such as the Devil's Advocate, you can bluff the Squid Girl: if you are executed but don't die, it helps prove you are the Squid Girl.

If a night passes with no deaths, you can claim to be the Squid Girl. This gives a plausible reason for the quiet night, and also raises the idea that all the Townsfolk are drunk.

scarecrow.ability: You think you are a Townsfolk character, but you are not. If you die, the next execution doesn't kill.
scarecrow.summary: The Scarecrow thinks they are a Townsfolk; after the Scarecrow dies, the next executed player is protected.
scarecrow.examples:
The Scarecrow thinks they are the Noble. On the first day, the Scarecrow dies by execution. On the second day, the Baron is executed but doesn't die.

The Scarecrow thinks they are the Fortune Teller. On the third night, the Scarecrow dies. The next day, the Butler is executed but doesn't die.
scarecrow.tips:
The Scarecrow doesn't know they are the Scarecrow. As long as the Scarecrow is on the script, if your character is a Townsfolk, you might be the Scarecrow!

If an execution kills a player, no Townsfolk who died before it was the Scarecrow. If an execution doesn't kill anyone, the player who died last night or was executed yesterday may be the Scarecrow.

If you are the Demon, you can usually spot the Scarecrow quickly, since the Scarecrow always reports false information or their ability misbehaves. Killing them at the right moment can protect you or a teammate. Sometimes it can also make a good player who was going to be executed need executing a second time, wasting one of good's executions.
scarecrow.bluffing:
Bluffing the Scarecrow is very hard. First you have to bluff a Townsfolk, then show that your ability doesn't work properly — which looks just like an evil player. You may be executed as a lying evil player.

A player bluffing the Scarecrow doesn't have the Scarecrow's ability, so after you die, nobody survives an execution. That makes you look even more like an evil player.

The Scarecrow can be a last excuse: if your claimed character is questioned for its ability not working, you can argue that you might be the Scarecrow.

rascal.ability: On your 1st night & 1st day, Townsfolk abilities yield false info.
rascal.summary: On the Rascal's first day in play, every Townsfolk goes wrong.
rascal.examples:
The Rascal is in play. On the first night, the Chef, the Empath, the Seamstress and every other Townsfolk who gets information learns false information.

The Rascal is in play. On the first day, the Savant gets 2 false statements.
rascal.tips:
If you are the Rascal, you had better reveal your character quickly! Your ability causes a lot of interference.

If you are the Rascal, you can talk to an important player you think is trustworthy and agree to claim each other's characters. That gets the news that the Rascal is in play out in time, and lets you cover for them and help them survive into the middle and late game.

If you are the Rascal: in most cases, being executed doesn't undo your negative effect, because even if you aren't executed on the first day, your ability's effect ends at nightfall.
rascal.bluffing:
If you are a Minion and you are sure the Rascal is not in play, announce that you are the Rascal! It will cause good a lot of trouble.

If you are the Demon, be careful about bluffing the Rascal: once good finds that the first night's information wasn't false, they may execute you immediately.

loverbound.ability: On your 1st night, choose a player (not yourself): after either of you dies, the other might die at any time.
loverbound.summary: The Loverbound and their lover might die at any time after the other dies.
loverbound.examples:
On the first night, the Loverbound chooses the Fortune Teller. On the second night, the Loverbound dies. On the fifth night, the Fortune Teller dies.

On the first night, the Loverbound chooses the Baron. On the third day, the Baron dies by execution. That night, the Loverbound dies.
loverbound.tips:
If you are the Loverbound, talk with your "lover" and look after each other, so that neither drags the other down.

If you are the Loverbound, be careful about revealing who your "lover" is: the Demon may deliberately kill one of you.

If you are the Demon, working out whom the Loverbound chose matters. You can kill one of them at the right moment in the hope that the other follows.
loverbound.bluffing:
Bluffing the Loverbound can explain some strange deaths — but only once you are already dead.

The Loverbound works as a backup bluff: when all your other bluffs have failed, you can reveal that you are really the Loverbound.

visagiste.ability: If a player you nominate, or who nominates you, is a Minion or Demon, that night they may choose to become a not-in-play character of the same type, even if you are dead.
visagiste.summary: A Demon or Minion who takes part in a nomination with the Visagiste can change their character.
visagiste.examples:
On the first day, the Visagiste nominates the Vortox. That night, the Vortox chooses to become the Fang Gu.

On the second day, the Fang Gu nominates the Visagiste. That night, the Fang Gu chooses to become the No Dashii.

On the third day, the Baron nominates the dead Visagiste. That night, the Baron chooses to become the Poisoner.
visagiste.tips:
If you are the Visagiste, don't reveal your character lightly, or your ability may well be exploited.

If you are the Visagiste, remember: as long as nobody nominates you and you nominate nobody, your ability can't trigger.

If you are the Visagiste and a player suddenly nominates you for no reason — especially after you have revealed yourself as the Visagiste — you have reason to believe they are a Minion or the Demon.

If you are a Minion, you can use the Visagiste's ability to change your character, as long as you know who the Visagiste is.

If you are the Demon, don't expose yourself just to use the Visagiste's ability. Make sure you have a solid reason for your nomination, or find a way to get the Visagiste to nominate you.
visagiste.bluffing:
The Visagiste is very careful about nominating. If you want to bluff the Visagiste, avoid nominating other players lightly; it makes you look more believable.

Use the Visagiste as a backup bluff. The Visagiste always tends to hide their character, so after your first bluff fails you can reveal that you are really the Visagiste — and even accuse the players who nominated you of being Minions or the Demon.

kappa.ability: On Judgment Day, you may learn from the Storyteller how many players are Outsiders. [Any number of Outsiders]
kappa.summary: The Kappa might change the number of Outsiders.
kappa.examples:
A 12-player game. The Kappa is in play and removed an Outsider, so the Kappa is the only Outsider. On Judgment Day, the Kappa visits the Storyteller and learns "1".

A 12-player game. The Kappa is in play and added 3 Outsiders, so there are 4 Outsiders. On Judgment Day, the Kappa is already dead, so they can't learn how many players are Outsiders.

A 12-player game. The Kappa is in play and didn't change the Outsider count, so there are 2 Outsiders. On Judgment Day, the Kappa visits the Storyteller and learns "2".
kappa.tips:
If you are the Kappa, it is best to reveal quickly that you are the Kappa, so everyone knows the Outsider count may have changed.

If you are the Kappa, you can hide your character until you learn the number of Outsiders in play, which keeps the Demon from learning you are the Kappa and killing you.

If you are evil and you know the Kappa is in play, you can try bluffing an Outsider.

If you are evil and you know the Kappa is not in play, you can bluff the Kappa and have your teammates bluff Outsiders too.

If you are the Demon, it is best to kill the Kappa before Judgment Day, so they don't learn how many players are Outsiders — especially while your teammates are bluffing Outsiders.
kappa.bluffing:
Bluffing the Kappa while your teammates bluff other Outsiders is a very good tactic.

Bluffing the Kappa makes every Outsider claim shaky: logically, any of them could be an evil bluff.

Before bluffing the Kappa, try to work out whether the Kappa is in play, so that you don't collide with the real one.

sphinx.ability: Each night, choose a character: tomorrow, if it is in play, that player is publicly asked a yes/no question. A player who doesn't answer correctly might be executed.
sphinx.summary: The Sphinx has the Storyteller question a particular character; a player who fails to answer correctly is executed.
sphinx.examples:
On the first night, the Sphinx chooses the Slayer, who is not in play. The next day, nobody is questioned.

On the first night, the Sphinx chooses the Slayer; Alex is the Slayer. The next day, after all nominations, the Storyteller asks everyone to be quiet and asks Alex: "Is the Gambler in play?" Alex answers "yes". The Gambler is in play, so nothing happens.

On the first night, the Sphinx chooses the Slayer; Alex is the Slayer. The next day, after all nominations, the Storyteller asks everyone to be quiet and asks Alex: "Is the Gambler in play?" Alex answers "yes". The Gambler is not in play, and the Storyteller decides that Alex is executed immediately. The Storyteller then declares nightfall.

On the first night, the Sphinx chooses the Slayer; Alex is the Slayer. The next day, before nominations begin, the Storyteller asks everyone to be quiet and asks Alex: "Is the Gambler in play?" Alex answers "yes". The Gambler is not in play, but the Storyteller decides not to execute Alex, so nothing happens.

On the third night, the Sphinx chooses the Sphinx. The next day, after all nominations, the Storyteller asks everyone to be quiet and asks the Sphinx: "Are you the Demon?" The Sphinx answers "yes" and is executed immediately. The Storyteller then declares nightfall.
sphinx.tips:
One use of the Sphinx is finding any character you want. If you fear the Fortune Teller, choose the Fortune Teller: if the Storyteller questions nobody the next day, the Fortune Teller is not in play. If the Storyteller does question a player, that player is certainly the Fortune Teller.

Good players usually reveal their character after being questioned. Choosing a teammate's character can help their bluff and make them look more believable.

At the right moments, you can deliberately choose a character that is not in play, to make it look as if the Sphinx is not in play or is already dead, and so confuse good.

If you would like the Storyteller to execute a questioned player who answers wrongly, you can signal this to the Storyteller at night or during the day. The Storyteller will take your view into account where they can (not always).

If you have come up with some brilliant questions, you can pass them to the Storyteller in any form, during the day or at night. The Storyteller will take your ideas into account where they can (not always).

If you are a good player questioned by the Sphinx, it is best to reveal your character, since the Sphinx already knows from who was questioned that you are the character they chose.

If you are a good player and you survive a question, your answer wasn't necessarily right. But if you were executed, you certainly answered wrongly.

leper_gnome.ability: When a Townsfolk player chooses you with their own ability, they immediately become a Leper Gnome, and you lose all your abilities. You win or lose with evil, even if you are dead.
leper_gnome.summary: Townsfolk who touch the Leper Gnome become Leper Gnomes too.
leper_gnome.examples:
On the first night, the Seamstress chooses the Leper Gnome. The Seamstress becomes a Leper Gnome, and the original Leper Gnome loses their ability. When the game ends, evil wins, and the new Leper Gnome (the former Seamstress) wins too.

On the first day, the Bard publicly chooses several players including the Leper Gnome. The Bard becomes a Leper Gnome, and the original Leper Gnome loses their ability. When the game ends, good wins, and the new Leper Gnome (the former Bard) loses because of their own ability.

On the second night, the Innkeeper chooses the original Leper Gnome. The Innkeeper becomes a Leper Gnome, and the original Leper Gnome loses their ability. Then the Seamstress chooses the Leper Gnome (the former Innkeeper): the Seamstress becomes a Leper Gnome too, and the Leper Gnome (former Innkeeper) loses their ability. Then the Chambermaid chooses the Leper Gnome (former Seamstress) and also becomes a Leper Gnome, and the Leper Gnome (former Seamstress) loses their ability. When the game ends, evil wins. The Leper Gnome (former Chambermaid) wins too because of their ability; the Leper Gnomes who were the Innkeeper and the Seamstress lose.
leper_gnome.tips:
If you are an evil Leper Gnome, do everything you can to tempt Townsfolk into choosing you with their abilities! Spread your leprosy! That is how you make yourself useful!

If you are a good Leper Gnome, first understand this: becoming a Leper Gnome doesn't change your alignment! You are still good. But the Leper Gnome's ability may mean you need to side with evil.

If you went from Townsfolk to Leper Gnome, think hard about whom you are fighting for now. If you can be sure no other Townsfolk has chosen you — meaning you still have your ability — you can win with evil through the Leper Gnome's ability. But if another Townsfolk has chosen you, you have lost your ability and still need to work for good! Unfortunately, you don't know whether you still have your ability. Think hard and judge carefully!

dark_knight.ability: Each night*, you learn which Outsider players died today, and guess their characters: if you guess correctly, a player dies. [+1 Outsider]
dark_knight.summary: The Dark Knight uses dead Outsiders to kill other players.
dark_knight.examples:
On the first day, the Butler dies. That night the Dark Knight is woken and learns the Butler player (the Storyteller points to them). The Dark Knight guesses the Butler, and the Dark Knight kills the Fortune Teller.

On the second night, the Imp attacks the Butler, who dies. That night the Dark Knight is woken and learns the Butler player (the Storyteller points to them). The Dark Knight guesses the Butler, and the Dark Knight kills the Saint.

On the first day, the Butler dies. That night the Imp attacks the Saint, who dies. That night the Dark Knight is woken and learns the Butler and Saint players (the Storyteller points to them). The Dark Knight guesses the Butler and the Saint, and kills the Fortune Teller.
dark_knight.tips:
If you are the Dark Knight, keep track of the Outsiders at all times, so that you can guess correctly when one dies.

If you are the Dark Knight and you are woken and shown a player, they are certainly an Outsider. You can guess wrongly on purpose to mislead good about which Minions are in play.

If you are the Dark Knight and your team needs several players dead, you can have the Demon attack an Outsider at night, so that together you deal with several players in one night.

If you are a good player: the Dark Knight adds Outsiders. If there are more Outsiders than you expected, the Dark Knight may be in play.

If you are an Outsider, keep your character hidden! Don't reveal it lightly, or the Dark Knight will use your death to attack other players.

narcotizer.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned until you choose someone else. When an alive player poisoned by you becomes healthy, they learn that the Narcotizer is in play.
narcotizer.summary: The Narcotizer poisons players, who find out once they are healthy again.
narcotizer.examples:
On the first night, the Narcotizer chooses the Noble, who is poisoned and gets false information. On the second night, the Narcotizer chooses the Fortune Teller. The Noble is still alive, so the Noble learns that the Narcotizer is in play.

On the first night, the Narcotizer chooses the Noble, who is poisoned and gets false information. On the first day, the Noble dies by execution. On the second night, the Narcotizer chooses the Fortune Teller, who is poisoned and gets false information.

On the first night, the Narcotizer chooses the Noble, who is poisoned and gets false information. On the second night, the Narcotizer chooses themself (since the Narcotizer is now poisoned, the Noble doesn't learn the Narcotizer is in play even though they are alive). On the third night, the Narcotizer chooses the Fortune Teller (skip the step where the Narcotizer would learn the Narcotizer is in play); the Fortune Teller is poisoned and gets false information.
narcotizer.tips:
If you are the Narcotizer: choosing a new player while the player you poisoned is still alive exposes you! That is a big disadvantage. If you don't want to reveal that the Narcotizer is in play, wait until they die before choosing someone new.

If you are the Narcotizer and you want to move your poison without being exposed, choose yourself, then choose a new target the next night. The downside is that on the night you choose yourself, nobody else is poisoned by you.

If you are a good player, don't fear the Narcotizer too much. If nobody learns the Narcotizer is in play, their poison can only spread in very limited ways. If you think you are poisoned by the Narcotizer, then until you die nobody else will be poisoned by them — unless you learn the Narcotizer is in play, or the Narcotizer wastes a night moving their poison.

If you are a good player and you learn the Narcotizer is in play, tell everyone as soon as it is day! It is very important: it means not only that the Narcotizer is in play, but that you were poisoned by the Narcotizer before, and that since last night a new player is poisoned by them!

doll.ability: You think you are a good character, but you are not. If the Demon kills you, the Demon chooses a player: they become the Doll. [The Doll neighbours the Demon]
doll.summary: The Doll doesn't know they are the Doll. The Demon can kill the old Doll to make a new one.
doll.examples:
The Doll thinks they are the Slayer and publicly chooses the Demon during the day. Nothing happens, since the Doll isn't really the Slayer.

At night the Demon kills the Doll and chooses the Fortune Teller, who becomes the new Doll (good). The Fortune Teller doesn't notice and still thinks they are the Fortune Teller, since the Doll thinks they are a good character.

The Demon tells the Fortune Teller sitting next to them that the Fortune Teller is the Doll, an evil Minion. The Fortune Teller believes it and helps the Demon win. But the Fortune Teller was never the Doll.

On the second night, the Demon kills the original Doll (evil) and chooses the Fortune Teller, who becomes the Doll (good) without knowing it. On the third night, the Demon kills the former Fortune Teller (now a good Doll) and chooses the Oracle, who becomes the Doll (good) without knowing it. On the fourth night, the Demon kills the former Oracle (now a good Doll) and chooses the Noble, who becomes the Doll (good) without knowing it.
doll.tips:
If you are the original Doll, the Demon is certainly sitting next to you.

If you can be sure neither player beside you is the Demon, you can all but conclude that whoever told you that you are the Doll is lying — expose them. Or you may already have been chosen by the Demon as a new Doll. Tell the difference carefully!

As the original Doll, you are essentially an evil Drunk: you not only lack the ability you think you have, you aren't even the alignment you think you are! The good news is that many of the tricks for checking whether you are the Drunk also work for the Doll. If your information doesn't make sense, or your ability didn't work when it should have, you may be the Doll rather than a good player!

If a player next to you says you are the Doll and then you die at night, the Demon is probably using their ability to make a new Doll. That isn't certain, though. Stay alert, and use your information to judge whether you really are the original Doll.

The number of Minions is fixed: a 12-player game has only 2 Minions. If you find that both the Baron and the Goblin are in play, you can hardly be the Doll.

If you are sure you aren't the Doll but someone tells you that you are, tell the group. The group will probably execute your neighbour, which means either a Demon dies, or a Minion, or a good player whose bluff was useless — at worst, a good player fooling around.

If you are good and a player next to you doesn't trust you much, tell them they are the Doll! For a while at least, most players will cooperate with you and try to work out their own characters. Just make sure that before the game ends, they understand they must cooperate with you to win.

Should I tell other players they are the Doll? Anyone can tell anyone they are the Doll. If you are a Minion hoping to get more good players working for evil, you can tell your neighbour that you are the Demon and they are the Doll.

If you are the Demon, nothing stops you telling your good neighbours they are the Doll. In fact, you can tell both of them, so that each is convinced they are the "real" Doll and the other has been fooled!

What does finding the Doll give good? If you find the original Doll, the Demon is certainly one of their neighbours! If you find a suspected new Doll made by the Demon, the previous Doll must have been killed by the Demon on some earlier night. If only one player has died at night so far, that player was the original Doll, and the Demon must be sitting next to them!

The Demon can only make one new Doll per night, and only after killing all the old Dolls. Keep this in mind: if you suspect there have been several Dolls, the chain of Dolls leaves a trail. Try to unravel it to find the Demon behind it.

If you think a player has been turned into the Doll, they no longer have an ability, and neither their ability nor their information can be trusted.

puck.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a non-Demon character: they die. If that character is not in play, also choose a player: they become that character.
puck.summary: The Puck loves wiping out characters they dislike, or conjuring up characters they like.
puck.examples:
Second night: the Puck chooses the Fortune Teller, who is in play and dies.

Second night: the Puck chooses the Fortune Teller, who is not in play. The Storyteller asks the Puck to choose a player too; the Puck chooses themself and becomes the Fortune Teller (evil).

Second night: the Puck chooses the Sweetheart, who is not in play. The Storyteller asks the Puck to choose a player too; the Puck chooses the Baron, who becomes the Sweetheart (evil).
puck.tips:
If you are the Puck and your team is desperate to kill a particular important character, you can remove that character with pinpoint precision.

If you are the Puck, you can turn yourself or a teammate into a not-in-play character at any time to gain its ability. Become the Dreamer or the Cyclops and check other players! Or become the Bard and start making Townsfolk drunk at will — also a fine choice! You can even cosplay your partner-in-mischief, the Wishing Fairy! The possibilities are endless: become the Hell's Outcast to move the Demon! Become the Heiress and let others die for you! Become the Sweetheart to make someone drunk! Become the Perfumer, give a good player a whiff, then have the Demon claim to be the Perfumer! Become Don Quixote! Become the Cowboy! There are too many ways to play — let your imagination run wild!

If you are the Puck and your teammates include the Ettins, turning one Ettin into another character both avoids the Ettins' drawback and gains another character's ability — two birds with one stone.

If you are the Puck, you can't create a Demon directly, but if needed you can turn yourself or another Minion into the Hell's Outcast and use the Hell's Outcast's ability to move the Demon. Only do this if you are sure the Hell's Outcast is not in play, or you will simply kill them.

If you are the Puck, turning yourself into the Wishing Fairy can also move the Demon — or, to be exact, get you anything at all, as long as you can meet the Storyteller's conditions.

If you are a good player and an Outsider claims to have learned that the Cyclops is in play but there is no extra Outsider, or you are sure the Ettins are in play but can never find which 2 players they are, consider the Puck! The Puck may have quietly changed some players' characters!

If a particularly important Townsfolk dies on the first day, especially one who hadn't told anyone their character, consider whether it was the Puck's doing!

Because of the Puck, you may not be able to fully trust players who have "proved" themselves with their abilities — the Perfumer, the Cowboy, the Ranger or the Heiress, say — since they may be evil players the Puck created!

codex.ability: Once per game, on your Xth night, choose players X times in total: they are poisoned until dusk. Players chosen more than once die instead.
codex.summary: On one night, the CodeX causes mass poisoning, even death. The more nights they have been through, the stronger they are.
codex.examples:
On the first night, the CodeX chooses the Noble once, and the Noble is poisoned and gets false information. The CodeX is not woken again on later nights.

On the first night, the CodeX doesn't use their ability. On the second night, the CodeX chooses the Fortune Teller and the Undertaker once each; both are poisoned and get false information. The CodeX is not woken again on later nights.

On the first and second nights, the CodeX doesn't use their ability. On the third night, the CodeX chooses the Fortune Teller once and the Undertaker twice. The Fortune Teller is poisoned and gets false information, and the Undertaker dies. The CodeX is not woken again on later nights.

Before the fifth night, the CodeX doesn't use their ability. On the fifth night, the CodeX chooses the Fortune Teller once, the Undertaker twice and the Drunk twice. The Fortune Teller is poisoned and gets false information; the Undertaker and the Drunk die. The CodeX is not woken again on later nights.

On the 4th night, the Puck turns themself into the CodeX, but the Storyteller signals that they can choose at most once, since tonight is their first night as the CodeX.
codex.tips:
The CodeX's ability grows stronger as the game goes on. You can use it early to shape the game, or save it to settle things late.

Early in the game your poisoning matters most, but you can only choose a few players. In the middle and late game your poisoning matters less, but you can choose lots of players. Picking the right moment to use your ability is the key skill of the CodeX.

The CodeX has to spend 2 choices to cause a death. If the CodeX kills a player on the second night, nobody is poisoned by the CodeX all game.

However the CodeX uses their ability, its effect lasts at most one day. Find the most likely day and check that day's information and deaths carefully.

If the CodeX uses their ability to poison players during the first 2 nights, they can't cause a death. If you are sure the CodeX is in play and there has been no suspicious death, then on some night the CodeX poisoned players.

A player killed by the CodeX is certainly not poisoned by the CodeX. If you suspect a player was killed by the CodeX, they were certainly not poisoned by the CodeX.

cyclops.ability: Each night, choose a player: you & the Demon learn their character. If you choose an Outsider, they learn that the Cyclops is in play. [+1 Outsider]
cyclops.summary: Each night, the Cyclops checks another player's character.
cyclops.examples:
The Cyclops is in play, so there is 1 more Outsider than the default. On the first night, the Cyclops chooses player 1, the Seamstress: the Cyclops and the Demon learn that player 1 is the Seamstress. On the first day, the Demon claims to be the Dreamer and correctly names player 1 as the Seamstress.

On the first night, the Cyclops chooses player 1, the Recluse: the Cyclops and the Demon learn that player 1 is the Recluse. The Recluse learns that the Cyclops is in play.

On the second night, the Cyclops chooses player 1, the Sage: the Cyclops and the Demon learn that player 1 is the Sage. That night the Demon doesn't kill the Sage and chooses another player instead.
cyclops.tips:
Check players who seem to be important characters first: knowing who the important characters are is key intelligence.

Check the strongest players first: knowing their characters and allegiance helps you read the game.

Avoid checking players who might be Outsiders: it would reveal that the Cyclops is in play and how many Outsiders there are.

Remember that your intelligence is shared with the Demon, who will choose whom to kill based on it. You and the Demon can work in step without even talking — that is the power of your ability.

If the Cyclops is not in play, you can openly claim to be an Outsider, and even claim to have learned that the Cyclops is in play. If good believes the Cyclops is in play, you will most likely survive to the end. The downside: if good becomes sure there is no Cyclops, you will immediately be taken for evil.

If an Outsider claims the Cyclops is in play and there is 1 more Outsider than the default, there are only 2 possibilities: either the Cyclops really is in play and the Outsiders are all good (unless the Chimera is in play), or the Outsider claiming the Cyclops is evil and the Cyclops is not in play.

Watch the number of Outsiders in play. If it is above the default, the Cyclops may well be in play even if no Outsider has learned it.

ettin.ability: If you die, the other Ettins die that night. The Ettins' votes only count if all Ettins vote together. [+1 Ettin (you choose who)]
ettin.summary: The Ettin gives the evil team an extra Minion; the two Ettins are a symbiotic pair who must vote together.
ettin.examples:
On the first night, the Ettin chooses the Seamstress, who becomes another evil Ettin, and the 2 Ettins learn each other. They are then woken together for the Minion info and learn the other Minions and the Demon.

On the first night, the Ettin chooses the Demon or a Minion. To stop the game ending outright, the Storyteller shakes their head and has the Ettin choose again.

During a vote, one Ettin raises their hand and the other doesn't. When the Storyteller counts the last voter, the count reaches 8, but the Storyteller announces that the player got 7 votes.

Alice and Bob are both Ettins. Bob is killed by the Demon at night, and Alice dies that night too.

An Ettin dies by execution, and the other Ettin dies that night.

An Ettin is killed by the Demon at night, and the other Ettin dies that night too.

The players try to test whether 2 players are Ettins by pressuring one to vote and the other not to. The Storyteller's advice is ignored: one Ettin votes and the other doesn't, but the Storyteller counts the Ettins' votes normally. (See the rules details for this case.)
ettin.tips:
The Ettin in play means evil has an extra Minion! That is a huge boost for evil, so coordinate well with your "brother"! The 2 of you bring evil extra nominations and a voting advantage — united, you are very strong!

Always watch whether your "brother" votes, and follow their lead. If you split your votes, you reveal that the Ettin is in play, and good may well work out from the votes which 2 players are the Ettins.

If you are the Ettin, choose a player you think is strong! Making them your "brother" is a big help to evil!

You and your "brother" share one mind, but most of the time you'd better not look too friendly! That makes it easier to spot that you are the Ettins.

If you are an Ettin, living and dying together isn't always bad: dying at the right moment can help evil with some special goals! For example, if 5 players are alive and 2 of them are Ettins, today is the final day! Whether one Ettin dies by execution or the Demon kills one at night, only 2 players will be alive the next day, which ends the game. You can also die at the right moment to pass as the Gambler, or to help a teammate pass as a character that causes extra deaths, like the Heiress or the Ranger.

If in a vote the count the Storyteller announces doesn't match the number of voters, one of the voters is certainly an Ettin! And the other Ettin is among the players who didn't vote!

If you suspect the Ettin is in play, they are among pairs of players who always vote together or always abstain together!

Don't force other players to vote or not vote to test whether they are Ettins! In that situation the Storyteller counts the Ettins' votes normally!

When one Ettin dies, the other dies that night! If you suspect a player is an Ettin, the best move is to try executing them! If an execution leads to an unusual death that night, the other Ettin is likely among that night's dead.

In most cases, the Ettin turns a Townsfolk or Outsider into the other Ettin at the start of the game. If the number of Outsiders doesn't match the default, consider this!

hekatonkheires.ability: If you publicly declare that you are the Hekatonkheires immediately after dying by execution, your next vote counts as the number of votes you received today.
hekatonkheires.summary: The more votes the Hekatonkheires receives, the more powerful their ability becomes.
hekatonkheires.examples:
On the first day, the Hekatonkheires gets 12 votes and dies by execution, and immediately after learning of their death publicly declares that they are the Hekatonkheires. On the final day, the Hekatonkheires votes with their vote token; when the Storyteller reaches the Hekatonkheires in the count, they count it as 12 votes. That day a good player gets 14 votes in total and dies by execution, and evil wins.

On the first day, the Hekatonkheires gets 12 votes and dies by execution, but does not publicly declare that they are the Hekatonkheires. On the final day, the Hekatonkheires votes with their vote token; when the Storyteller reaches them in the count, it counts as 1 vote as usual.

On the fourth day, the Hekatonkheires gets 4 votes and dies by execution, and immediately after learning of their death publicly declares that they are the Hekatonkheires. The next day, the Hekatonkheires votes with their vote token; when the Storyteller reaches them in the count, it counts as 4 votes.
hekatonkheires.tips:
If you are the Hekatonkheires, rack your brains for ways to die by execution early.

If you are the Hekatonkheires, make your bluff as absurd as you can. If good sees through it and executes you, wonderful. If good doesn't see through it, the bluff has worked anyway.

If you are the Hekatonkheires, think carefully about whether to declare yourself. Usually, if early in the game you got enough votes to dominate an execution, declare without hesitation. In the middle or late game, if declaring would only get you 3 or 4 votes, think hard about whether it is worth it: declaring certainly reveals you as evil, which usually hurts the evil team.

If you are another Minion, declaring yourself the Hekatonkheires when you die by execution can also be a workable tactic. You don't really gain the Hekatonkheires's ability, but good will be very wary of you, especially if you got a lot of votes.

If you are good: if no player has declared themself the Hekatonkheires after dying by execution, no Hekatonkheires's ability can have triggered.

If you are good and a player declares themself the Hekatonkheires after dying by execution, remember how many votes they got that day. If they really are the Hekatonkheires, evil can add that many votes to any execution on any day. Prepare accordingly.

clone.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a player: they die, and you become their character.
clone.summary: The Clone kills players and becomes their copy.
clone.examples:
On the second night, the Clone chooses the Fortune Teller player. The Fortune Teller dies and the Clone becomes the Fortune Teller.

On the second night, the Clone chooses the Golem player. The Golem dies and the Clone becomes the Golem. The next day, the new Golem nominates the Fortune Teller, who dies.

On the fourth night, the Clone chooses the Vortox player. The Vortox dies and the Clone becomes the Vortox. The Vortox has already acted that night, so the new Vortox is not woken again.

On the fourth night, the Clone chooses the Saint player, who is protected by the Innkeeper. The Saint doesn't die, and the Clone doesn't become the Saint.

On the fourth night, the Clone chooses the dead Fang Gu. The Fang Gu can't die again, and the Clone doesn't become the Fang Gu.
clone.tips:
If you are the Clone, you can use your ability to kill important characters, or use its killing power to pass as another character, such as the Gossip or the Gambler.

If you are the Clone, the new character you become tells you what character the player you killed was.

If you are the Clone, killing the Demon makes you the new Demon. Moving the Demon is an important use of your ability.

If you are the Clone, you can kill a player to take their ability. For example, kill the Poisoner and poison every night; kill the Snake Charmer to swap with the Demon whenever you like; or kill the Virgin, planning to waste one of good's executions.

If you are a good player, note that the Clone can kill the Demon and become the new Demon, moving the Demon. If there are unusually many deaths at night and one of them is your main suspect, they may be a Demon killed by the Clone.

If you are a good player and the unusual night deaths include characters whose abilities could strongly affect the game, like the Virgin or the Gossip, the Clone may have killed them and taken their ability. Watch out for the Clone using that new ability to do even more damage.

witch_doctor.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned & their death is delayed, until you choose someone else.
witch_doctor.summary: A player poisoned by the Witch Doctor has their death delayed until the Witch Doctor's protection ends.
witch_doctor.examples:
On the first night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Noble, who is poisoned and gets false information that night. The next day, the Noble is executed but doesn't die (delayed death). On the second night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Fortune Teller; the Noble's delayed death ends and the Noble dies.

On the second night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Fortune Teller, and the Demon attacks the Fortune Teller, who doesn't die because of the Witch Doctor's ability (delayed death); being poisoned, the Fortune Teller gets false information. The next day, the Fortune Teller is executed but doesn't die because of the Witch Doctor's ability (delayed death). On the third night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Fortune Teller again, who gets false information because they are poisoned. On a night with 4 players left, the Witch Doctor chooses themself: the Fortune Teller's delayed death ends and the Fortune Teller dies. The Demon kills another player. Only 2 players are alive, and evil wins.

On the fourth night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Imp. The Imp is poisoned and attacks the Fortune Teller that night, but because the Imp is poisoned, the Fortune Teller doesn't die. The next day, the Imp is executed but doesn't die (delayed death). On the fifth night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Imp again, and the Imp's death stays delayed. The next day, the Witch Doctor is executed: the Imp's delayed death ends, and the Witch Doctor and the Imp die together. Good wins.

On the first night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Monk, who is poisoned. On the first day, the Monk is executed but doesn't die (delayed death). On the second day, the Witch Doctor is executed: the Monk's delayed death ends, and the Witch Doctor and the Monk die together.

On the second night, the Witch Doctor chooses the Banshee, and the Imp attacks the Banshee, who doesn't die (delayed death). On the third night, the Witch Doctor chooses another player and the Banshee dies. The Banshee's ability doesn't trigger, since the Banshee counts as killed by the Witch Doctor.

On the first night, the Witch Doctor chooses themself. Being poisoned, the Witch Doctor loses all their abilities, so they are not protected from death.
witch_doctor.tips:
Remember, your ability has at least 3 uses. First, poisoning to disrupt other players' abilities. Second, making an executed player not die (for now), to protect a particular player or fake another character's ability. Third, working with the Demon to push a night's death onto a later night, to fake a night with no deaths or for other purposes. Use your imagination and make the most of the Witch Doctor's ability for some brilliant plays!

If you want to choose the Demon, remember 2 things. First, your ability poisons the Demon, so they can't kill their target. Second, if the Demon is executed while under your protection, they don't die at once, but they die as soon as your protection ends.

You can choose the same target as the Demon at night to create a night with no deaths, then choose a new target on another night, making it look as if several players died on the same night.

If you are a good player and you think you are poisoned by the Witch Doctor, you can try executing yourself. If you die, you were certainly not poisoned by the Witch Doctor the night before.

If you are a good player and you were executed but didn't die, then died that night along with other players, you were most likely chosen by the Witch Doctor the night before, and they chose a new target that night.

If you are good and you have executed a suspected Demon several times without them dying, and the nights have had no deaths, a Witch Doctor is very likely keeping the Demon alive from the shadows. Stop executing them and go find and execute that hidden Witch Doctor.

The Witch Doctor can't protect themself. If you find the Witch Doctor, execute them quickly.

venomtail.ability: The 1+X nearest Townsfolk clockwise from you are poisoned. [No Outsiders in play. X is how many Outsiders you removed]
venomtail.summary: The Venomtail turns Outsiders into poisoned Townsfolk, trailing a "poison" tail behind them.
venomtail.examples:
A 12-player game. The Venomtail removed 2 Outsiders, so 1+2 = 3 Townsfolk are poisoned. The Venomtail is player 1, so players 2 (the Fortune Teller), 3 (the Innkeeper) and 4 (the Ravenkeeper) are poisoned.

A 12-player game with the Venomtail and the Fang Gu (+1 Outsider) in play. The Venomtail removed 3 Outsiders, so 1+3 = 4 Townsfolk are poisoned. The Venomtail is player 1 and the Fang Gu player 2, so players 3 (the Fortune Teller), 4 (the Innkeeper), 5 (the Ravenkeeper) and 6 (the Washerwoman) are poisoned.

A 12-player game with the Venomtail and the Vigormortis (-1 Outsider) in play. The Venomtail removed 1 Outsider, so 1+1 = 2 Townsfolk are poisoned. The Venomtail is player 1 and the Vigormortis player 2, so players 3 (the Fortune Teller) and 4 (the Innkeeper) are poisoned.

A 10-player game. The Venomtail removed no Outsiders, so 1+0 = 1 Townsfolk is poisoned. The Venomtail is player 1, the Imp player 2 and the Scarlet Woman player 3. Player 4 (the Fortune Teller) is poisoned.

A 10-player game. The Venomtail removed no Outsiders, so 1+0 = 1 Townsfolk is poisoned. The Venomtail is player 1, so player 2 (the Fortune Teller) is poisoned. On the second night, the Pit-Hag turns player 2 into an Outsider. Since player 2 is no longer a Townsfolk, player 3 (the Empath) is poisoned from now on.
venomtail.tips:
If you are the Venomtail: no Outsiders are in play, which means you come with every Outsider as a ready-made bluff!

If you are the Venomtail, making the Outsider count look normal is your most important job! If nobody claims to be an Outsider, players will soon be sure the Venomtail is in play. If you don't want to bluff an Outsider yourself (once players are sure the Venomtail is in play, you are certainly evil and very likely the Venomtail, and following from you they will find every poisoned Townsfolk), have a teammate bluff an Outsider. Then even if the Venomtail is exposed, players can't use the fake Outsider's seat to quickly locate all the poisoned Townsfolk.

If you are the Venomtail, note that your death makes every Townsfolk you poisoned healthy again. If your teammates — especially the Demon — are among the players you poison, they can pretend to be poisoned by you, or made healthy by your death, to win other players' trust.

If you are an Outsider, the Venomtail is certainly not in play! Don't consider the Venomtail at all — at least at the start of the game, it definitely isn't there.

If you are a Townsfolk and you think the Venomtail is in play, any player claiming to be an Outsider is certainly evil! Try to execute them, and look for signs of poisoning clockwise from them.

If you are a Townsfolk and you and several Townsfolk near you seem to be poisoned, the Venomtail may be causing trouble "upstream" of you. Try to find and execute them: that makes you healthy again.

If you are a Townsfolk and you have found the Venomtail, the players "downstream" of them aren't necessarily all good! Other evil players may be hiding among them. Tell them apart carefully.

yuki_onna.ability: On your 1st night alive, and on your 1st night dead, choose a player: they are poisoned.
yuki_onna.summary: The Yuki-onna's bitter longing crosses life and death, bringing poison in each.
yuki_onna.examples:
On the first night, the Yuki-onna chooses the Fortune Teller, who is poisoned. On the third day, the Yuki-onna dies by execution and the Fortune Teller becomes healthy. That night, the Yuki-onna chooses the Fortune Teller again, who is poisoned.

On the first night, the Yuki-onna chooses the Noble, who is poisoned. On the second night, the Demon kills the Yuki-onna and the Noble becomes healthy. The Yuki-onna chooses the Fortune Teller, who is poisoned.

On the first night, the Yuki-onna chooses the Noble, who is poisoned. On the second night, the Yuki-onna dies because of the Gossip's ability and the Noble becomes healthy. The Yuki-onna chooses the Fortune Teller, who is poisoned.

On the first night, the Yuki-onna chooses the Fortune Teller, who is poisoned. The Yuki-onna stays alive all game, and the Fortune Teller stays poisoned throughout.
yuki_onna.tips:
If you are the Yuki-onna, on the first night choose a player who seems to have a strong character, or a player you think is very skilled! With no in-game information to go on, just choose boldly — it takes a little luck.

If you are the Yuki-onna and you find you poisoned an important player on the first night with a big effect, try not to die, to keep them poisoned. Of course, if you do die by accident, you can choose them again to keep them poisoned — but then you can't poison anyone else this game.

If you are the Yuki-onna and you find you poisoned an unimportant player while a more important player badly needs poisoning, find a way to die — ideally by execution, or failing that, by having the Demon kill you.

If you are a good player, remember: the Yuki-onna can only poison a new player after dying. So you needn't worry, as with the Poisoner, that a different player may be poisoned each day. At most 2 players are ever poisoned by the Yuki-onna, and only if the Yuki-onna dies.

If you are a good player: the Yuki-onna's first-night choice has little to go on — it is mostly blind. So an important player is unlikely to be poisoned on the first night. If an important player seems to be poisoned by the Yuki-onna, most likely the Yuki-onna died and then chose them. Try to find out which of the dead players is the Yuki-onna.

illus.ability: While both your neighbours are alive, Townsfolk abilities yield false info.
illus.summary: The Illus makes every Townsfolk get false information.
illus.examples:
The Illus is in play. On the first night, the Steward learns an evil player, the Fortune Teller chooses 2 non-Demon players but learns that one of them is the Demon, and the Seamstress chooses 2 players of the same alignment but learns they are different.

The Illus is in play. On the first night, every Townsfolk learns false information. On the second night, the Demon kills the Illus, and the Townsfolk no longer learn false information.

The Illus is in play. On the first night, every Townsfolk learns false information. On the second night, every Townsfolk learns false information. The next day, the Seamstress, who sits next to the Illus, dies by execution. That night, the Townsfolk no longer learn false information.
illus.tips:
If you are the Illus, tell your teammates you are the Illus, so that everyone can decide whether to put out "true" or "false" information.

If you are the Illus, report "true information" together with your teammates to hide that the Illus is in play! If good doesn't realise the Illus is in play, the false information the Townsfolk produce will badly mislead them!

If you are the Illus, don't worry if good becomes sure the Illus is in play and uses that as the basis for sorting out information. Even then, they can only get true information by flipping yes/no information; any other information is worth very little.

If you are the Illus, when necessary seek execution yourself, or even get the Demon to kill you. The Townsfolk's information then becomes true again, and if good doesn't correctly work out which day the Illus died, it causes huge confusion.

If you are evil and the Illus is not in play, try to convince everyone that it is! That turns most of the information in play into "false information" and causes huge confusion.

If you are good, don't fear the Illus too much. If you can be sure the Illus is in play, just read the information in reverse! What you should really watch for is whether the Illus died on some day, which would make the information turn true partway through.

If you are good, in scripts with the Illus, get into the habit of following 2 lines of reasoning: one where the Illus is in play and information is false, and one where it isn't and information is true.

shaman.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose 4 characters of different types: for each one not in play, a player of that type becomes that character.
shaman.summary: The Shaman can change many players' characters at once.
shaman.examples:
Second night: the Shaman chooses the Vortox, Poisoner, Saint and Fortune Teller, none of which is in play. The Fang Gu becomes the Vortox, the Baron becomes the Poisoner, the Butler becomes the Saint, and the Empath becomes the Fortune Teller.

Second night: the Shaman chooses the Vortox, Poisoner, Saint and Fortune Teller. The Vortox is not in play; the Poisoner, Saint and Fortune Teller are. The Fang Gu becomes the Vortox.

Third night: the Shaman chooses the Vortox, Poisoner, Saint and Fortune Teller. The Vortox and Fortune Teller are in play; the Poisoner and Saint are not. The Shaman becomes the Poisoner and the Ogre becomes the Saint.
shaman.tips:
If you are the Shaman, your ability is powerful: you can change which Demon is in play, change which Minions are in play, and create Outsiders that weren't in play — even all at once. But you only get one chance, so be careful.

If you are the Shaman and you use your ability early, you don't yet know which characters are in play, so you easily end up changing Townsfolk or Outsiders, which can expose you. If you use it in the middle or late game, you know much better what is in play and can control which types of character change and which don't.

If you are the Shaman and you change an Outsider or Townsfolk, the changed player will most likely announce that their character changed, exposing you. Be prepared for that. Though if that was your goal, their speaking up saves you the trouble of finding them.

If you are good and you have been turned into another character of the same type, the Shaman is very likely using their ability. Announce it quickly: the Minions and Demon have very likely changed too.

If you are good, don't fear the Shaman too much: the Shaman's ability is powerful, but they only get one chance.

If you are good and you think the Minion or Demon characters in play have changed, the Shaman may have used their ability. The Shaman can turn the Demon and Minions into not-in-play characters all at once.

versifier.ability: Each night, you learn a word (all from the same line of verse). The 1st time an alive player recites this line, they are executed immediately, even if you are dead.
versifier.summary: A player who recites the Versifier's line of verse is executed immediately.
versifier.examples:
The Versifier's line is "月落乌啼霜满天" ("The moon sets, crows caw, frost fills the sky"). On the first night, the Versifier learns "乌" (crow). On the second night, the Versifier learns "天" (sky). On the third night, the Versifier learns "月" (moon). The next day, the Versifier recites the whole line aloud and is executed immediately.

The Versifier's line is "牧童遥指杏花村" ("The shepherd boy points far off to Apricot Blossom Village"). On the first night, the Versifier learns "杏" (apricot). The next day, the Versifier dies by execution and gets no more words after that. On a day with 5 players alive, the alive Baron recites "一枝红杏出墙来" ("a branch of red apricot blossom reaches over the wall"): nothing happens. The Baron then recites "杏花零落水痕肥" ("apricot blossoms fall, the watermarks swell"): nothing happens. The Baron then recites "牧童遥指杏花村" and is executed immediately.

The Versifier's line is "烟蒲绿自生" ("misty rushes grow green of themselves"). A Townsfolk recites it aloud during the day and is executed immediately.
versifier.tips:
If you are the Versifier, your first job is to work out exactly which line of verse is yours. To do that, try to survive into the middle or late game; with only one or two words it is hard to pin down the line.

If you are the Versifier: even after you die, the forced-execution part of your ability still works, and you can still have a teammate recite the line to force an execution. Of course, tricking a good player into reciting it is even better.

crosswing.ability: On night X, choose whether the players X steps away from you are poisoned until dusk.
crosswing.summary: The Crosswing slowly unfolds, and every player it touches is poisoned.
crosswing.examples: First night: the Crosswing, player 6, is woken and nods to use their ability. The 2 players 1 step from player 6 — player 5, the Fortune Teller, and player 7, the Saint — are poisoned that night, until the end of the next day. Second night: the Crosswing is woken and nods. The 2 players 2 steps from player 6 — player 4, the Pit-Hag, and player 8, the Gossip — are poisoned that night, until the end of the next day. Third night: the Crosswing is woken and shakes their head, so the 2 players 3 steps from player 6 — player 3, the Imp, and player 9, the Banshee — are not poisoned.
crosswing.tips:
If you are the Crosswing, work out each night who would be poisoned by you! Try to poison Townsfolk and avoid poisoning anyone else, which causes lots of trouble — Outsider abilities stop working, or the Demon can't kill their target.

If you are the Crosswing and you notice good players trying to work out whether the Crosswing is in play, or where it sits, from whether their abilities fail, you can deliberately not poison them to throw off their reasoning.

If you are the Crosswing, note that once you are dead, nobody is poisoned by you. So try to survive into the late game.

If you are a good player: the Crosswing's poison is always symmetrical! If you think a player was poisoned by the Crosswing, you can use that to work out where the other poisoned player and the Crosswing sit.

If you are a Townsfolk: usually you can be poisoned by the Crosswing on at most one night, since the next night the poison moves past you. Remember this.

If you are a good player: a cunning Crosswing may deliberately skip their ability! If some players who should have been poisoned by the Crosswing have abilities that worked normally, that doesn't mean the Crosswing isn't in play!

dawnyx.ability: Good can't win while you are alive. A Demon who dies by execution regains their ability at dawn.
dawnyx.summary: The Dawnyx lets a dead Demon regain their ability at dawn.
dawnyx.examples:
First day: the Imp dies by execution, but because of the Dawnyx's ability the game doesn't end. On the second night, the Demon is dead, so nobody is killed. At dawn, the Imp regains their ability. On every night after that, the Imp attacks.

First day: the Imp dies by execution, but because of the Dawnyx's ability the game doesn't end. On the second day, the Dawnyx dies by execution and the game ends. Good wins.

On a day with only 4 players alive, the Demon dies by execution, but because the Dawnyx is alive, the game doesn't end. Nobody dies that night. The next day, 3 players are alive; a good player dies by execution, leaving only the Dawnyx and one other player alive. The game ends and evil wins.

On a day with only 3 players alive, the Demon and the Dawnyx are both alive. The Storyteller declares evil the winner early, because whoever is executed today, evil's win condition is met and good's can't be.
dawnyx.tips:
If you are the Dawnyx, try to survive to the end: you matter more than the Demon.

If you are the Dawnyx: usually, when your ability triggers, that night has no deaths. Find a way to cover this up.

If you are the Dawnyx: you don't register as the Demon, which is your advantage. Play a low-profile good player to survive to the final day.

If you are good: the Dawnyx's ability triggering usually comes with a night with no deaths. If you believe the Demon is already dead, find and execute the Dawnyx quickly.

If you are good and you find a player who might be the Dawnyx, deal with them first.

kitsune.ability: Each night*, choose a player & an Outsider character: if that character is not in play, they become it. If they are that character, they die. [-1 or +1 Outsider]
kitsune.summary: The Kitsune toys with all the Outsiders.
kitsune.examples:
Because the Kitsune is in play, there is 1 more Outsider than the default. On the second night, the Kitsune chooses the Baron player and the Saint. The Saint is not in play, so the Baron becomes the Saint. On the third night, the Kitsune chooses the Saint player (the former Baron) and the Saint, and the Saint dies.

Because the Kitsune is in play, there is 1 fewer Outsider than the default. On the second night, the Kitsune chooses the Fortune Teller player and the Saint. The Saint is in play, so nothing happens. On the third night, the Kitsune chooses the Fortune Teller player and the Sweetheart. The Sweetheart is not in play, so the Fortune Teller player becomes the Sweetheart. On the next night, the Kitsune chooses the Sweetheart player (the former Fortune Teller) and the Sweetheart: the Sweetheart dies, and a player becomes drunk because of the Sweetheart.
kitsune.tips:
If you are the Kitsune, note that turning good players into Outsiders exposes you. Of course you can ignore that risk: turning important Townsfolk into Outsiders to strip their abilities is also a good move.

If you are the Kitsune and you want to kill an Outsider, you have to guess their character. Some Outsiders may hide or lie about their characters to fool you — but if you made that Outsider yourself, they can't escape you!

If you are the Kitsune, note that your presence changes the default number of Outsiders in play. Find a way to cover this up.

If you are a good player and you have been turned into an Outsider, it was certainly the Kitsune's doing! Make it public as soon as you can.

If you are a good player and an Outsider dies unexpectedly at night, consider whether the Kitsune is in play. If it is, the starting number of Outsiders differs from the default. Check the Outsider count and see whether evil players are falsely claiming to be Outsiders!

yasha.ability: Each night*, you may choose a player you nominated, or who nominated you, today: they die.
yasha.summary: At night, the Yasha takes revenge on those it has a grudge against.
yasha.examples:
On the first day, the Yasha nominates the Fortune Teller. That night, the Yasha is woken and chooses the Fortune Teller, who dies.

On the second day, the Saint nominates the Yasha. That night, the Yasha is woken and chooses the Saint, who dies.

On the first day, the Yasha doesn't nominate and nobody nominates the Yasha. That night, the Yasha is not woken.
yasha.tips:
If you are the Yasha, try to take part in nominations, or get nominated by other players, so that you can use your ability.

If you are the Yasha, don't cause a death every day — it may be too obvious. Attack other players only now and then, so you look less like the Yasha.

If you are a good player, look at the nominations involving players who died unexpectedly at night, and see whether they all point to the same player. If so, that player is very likely the Yasha.

toxblast.ability: When a player is executed, their 2 Townsfolk neighbours are poisoned until dusk tomorrow. If nobody is executed today, all Townsfolk are poisoned until dusk tomorrow.
toxblast.summary: The Townsfolk next to an executed player are poisoned.
toxblast.examples:
On the first day, nobody is executed, so all Townsfolk are poisoned.

On the first day, the Noble is executed but doesn't die. The nearest Townsfolk to the Noble are the Fortune Teller and the Empath, sitting next to them, so the Fortune Teller and the Empath are poisoned.

On the third day, the Baron dies by execution. The nearest Townsfolk to them are the dead Noble and the dead King, so the dead Noble and the dead King are poisoned.
toxblast.tips:
If you are the Toxblast, watch each day's execution and work out which Townsfolk you have poisoned. They lose their ability or get false information, so you can prepare lies ahead of time that fit their information and make their abilities look normal.

If you are another evil player: the Toxblast is a strong deterrent even when not in play. Whether or not the Toxblast is in play, you can use "the Toxblast poisons the Townsfolk next to an executed player" to explain things away plausibly.

If you are a good player, plan each day's execution sensibly and keep in mind which players the Toxblast's poison may be on. If the players next to the executed player aren't Townsfolk, the Toxblast's poison skips them and lands on players further away. Don't overlook this.

twinflower.ability: You think you are a Townsfolk character, but you are not. [+1 Twinflower. The 2 Twinflowers neighbour each other]
twinflower.summary: The 2 Twinflowers sit next to each other, and both think they are Townsfolk.
twinflower.examples: A 12-player game with 3 Minions in play. The 2 Twinflowers sit next to each other and think they are the Fortune Teller and the Empath respectively.
twinflower.tips:
If you are a Twinflower, you don't learn that you are a Twinflower; you think you are a Townsfolk. If a player tells you that you are really a Twinflower, they may be lying — or you may really be a Twinflower. If you really are, you are an evil Minion.

If you are a Twinflower, the other Twinflower is certainly sitting next to you. If you suspect you are a Twinflower, find that other Twinflower: if both your abilities seem to fail, you are very likely both Twinflowers.

If you are a Twinflower and you suspect it, it is best to find the "twin" you suspect and talk it over together!

If you are a good player: the Twinflowers always sit next to each other and both think they are Townsfolk! If 2 neighbouring Townsfolk both have abilities going wrong, behaving inconsistently between the early, middle and late game, they are very likely the Twinflowers!

If you are another evil player, should you tell the Twinflowers what they are? It depends on the game. If things are going well for evil, you can hold off "waking" them for now. If not, find them and tell them the truth, so they can work hard for evil!

daruma.ability: If another player answers your question, they might die. If you answer another player's question, you might die. You can't die from anything else.
daruma.summary: Whoever pays the Daruma any attention meets with misfortune.
daruma.examples:
First day: the Daruma asks the Noble: "What's your character?" The Noble answers, and the Noble dies.

First day: the Daruma is executed, but doesn't die.

Second night: the Daruma asks aloud: "What day is it now?" The Fortune Teller answers, and the Fortune Teller dies.

Third day: the Saint asks the Daruma: "Did you order the takeaway at the door?" The Daruma answers, and the Daruma dies.
daruma.tips:
If you are the Daruma, you can start asking questions from the first day — ask like mad! As long as people keep answering you, you can keep causing deaths. Do everything you can to get other players to respond to you.

If you are the Daruma, you can keep your character hidden at first, then strike suddenly in the middle or late game and cause several deaths.

If you are the Daruma and you have been exposed, other players will avoid talking to you as much as they can. You need to act more naturally then: casual, everyday, simple questions asked out of the blue are often the ones that work.

If you are the Daruma, don't answer other players' questions! It is the only way to kill you.

If you are the Daruma, deliberately answering other players' questions in the middle or late game to seek death may help you win faster.

If you are a good player, don't answer the Daruma's questions — don't respond to them at all! At least once you know they are the Daruma.

If you are a good player and clever enough, you can trick the Daruma into answering your question. It may be difficult, but it is the only way to get rid of this pest for good!

cerberus.ability: Each night*, choose a player, and choose again each time you choose an evil player: they die. Minions you kill keep their ability.
cerberus.summary: The Cerberus can kill Minion after Minion, and those Minions keep their abilities.
cerberus.examples:
Second night: the Cerberus chooses the Chambermaid, who dies.

Second night: the Cerberus chooses the Mastermind, and the Storyteller signals the Cerberus to choose again. The Cerberus chooses the Chambermaid. The Mastermind and the Chambermaid die; the Mastermind keeps their ability despite being dead. The next day, the Cerberus is executed, but the game continues because of the Mastermind's ability. The day after, a good player is executed, the Mastermind's ability triggers, and so evil wins.

Second night: the Cerberus chooses the evil Ogre, and the Storyteller signals the Cerberus to choose again. The Cerberus chooses the Godfather, and the Storyteller signals again. The Cerberus chooses the Chambermaid. The Ogre, the Godfather and the Chambermaid die; the Godfather keeps their ability despite being dead.
cerberus.tips:
Your ability is vital to evil, and many tactics revolve around it — for example, causing extra deaths to help evil pass as the Gambler, the Gossip, the Heiress or the Wishing Fairy.

Killing Minions early keeps them from losing their abilities when they die, so that important Minion abilities last into the middle and late game.

Killing all your Minions in one go late in the game to end it early is also a good tactic.

If you are a good player and the Cerberus is in play, the players who die at night may include Minions. Work out which of them is the Minion and what ability they kept.

If you are a good player, you suspect the Cerberus is in play, and you think it hasn't killed its Minions, it may well be quietly gathering strength, planning to kill all its Minions in one go to end the game early. Find the Demon quickly, or the game may suddenly end on a night with 5–6 players alive.

siren.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die, and choose whether to permanently lose the ability that follows. Townsfolk abilities yield false info.
siren.summary: The Siren makes Townsfolk learn false information, and can drop that ability at any time.
siren.examples:
On the first night, the Noble learns 3 good players (false information).

On the first night, the Noble learns 3 good players (false information). On the second night, the Siren chooses to take a curtain call: from then on, Townsfolk abilities no longer give false information because of the Siren.

The Siren never takes a curtain call all game, so every Townsfolk gives false information throughout.
siren.tips:
If you are the Siren, taking your curtain call at the right moment is the key to winning!

If you are the Siren, you can also never take a curtain call. Good may wrongly assume you already have, and misjudge some information.

If you are a good player, don't fear the Siren: the key to spotting the Siren is the first night's information! With the Siren in play, the first night's information is certainly false!

If you are a good player: once the Siren takes a curtain call, she loses for good the ability to make Townsfolk give false information. If you believe the Siren has taken her curtain call, treat all information as true!
